features.title: Durable runtime and persistence
goals: Retain work, sessions, events and artifacts through interruptions with explicit durable outcomes.

requirements.text: ARCH-01 [Confirmed]: The app must own the runtime for its selected capabilities. It must not require CodeGraph, dark-factory, simple-router, MariaDB, RabbitMQ, Docker, or a VM to be installed and administered as supporting servers. Optional container runtimes used by managed projects are separate from this core-app constraint under CONTAINER-01–03.

ARCH-02 [Proposed]: UI actions and agent tools must call the same validated Rust application operations. Neither may bypass work-transition rules, revision checks, attribution, or durable history by directly editing storage.

ARCH-03 [Proposed]: Long-running indexing, provider calls, process output, graph work, and background jobs must not block the UI event loop. Components must publish observable state changes that update open screens incrementally.

ARCH-04 [Proposed]: App-managed child processes are allowed for repository commands and optional helpers. A worker process using the same shipped application is a possible isolation mechanism, not a required microservice or account boundary. Final process topology remains open.

ARCH-05 [Confirmed]: The core coordinator and worker harness must be implemented in the Rust application and use its router and tools directly. Running the app must not require a separately installed Claude Code, Codex CLI, or other external agent harness. Optional tool adapters must declare their own dependencies.
ARCH-06 [Confirmed]: The shipped native UI must use egui. Existing HTML artifacts remain design references; selecting egui does not convert the product into a web UI.

STORE-01 [Confirmed]: The normal desktop configuration must use local embedded storage and persistent in-process scheduling rather than requiring a database daemon or message broker. SQLite must support durable queueing, not just transient in-memory notifications.

STORE-02 [Proposed]: A durable queue must support bounded claims, ownership, renewable leases, cancellation, priority, retry policy, terminal failures, and visible status. Restarts must recover pending work without treating every abandoned attempt as safe to replay.

STORE-03 [Proposed]: Authoritative domain changes, related history and durable queued intent must commit atomically through the application transaction contract. Derived graph, lexical and vector indexes may be prepared asynchronously, with operation identity, idempotent application, generation publication and visible freshness. A saved record must not imply its derived index is already current; database, file and external effects require explicit reconciliation where atomic commit is unavailable.

STORE-04 [Confirmed]: Before retrying an interrupted push, merge, database write or other state-changing tool operation, reconcile what actually happened. Record confirmed completion rather than duplicating it; retry only when the observed state makes that safe. If the coordinator cannot determine an operation outcome, pause the affected operation and dependent work, notify the user and let unrelated work continue. Provider recovery must account for partial output and uncertain request/cost outcomes under existing router policy. Queue deduplication does not prove exactly-once external execution. Reconciliation does not bypass existing manual-resume rules.

STORE-05 [Proposed]: Manual backup and restore under STORE-07 must cover the application database or databases and referenced artifacts at a consistent checkpoint. Define visible scope selection and backup/export controls. Code-derived indexes may be rebuilt; authored knowledge, conversations, instructions, decisions, and execution history must not be treated as disposable indexes.

STORE-06 [Proposed]: Schema migrations must be versioned and checked before write access. Storage failure, disk exhaustion, incompatible versions, and incomplete recovery must be visible, with preserved data and a diagnosable recovery path.
STORE-07 [Confirmed]: Backups of application databases and artifact files must be initiated manually. Do not run automatic backups.

STORE-08 [Confirmed]: Use plain embedded SQLite with sqlite-vec for internal app storage. Persist graph nodes and edges in application-owned tables, with bounded graph traversal/analysis behind the storage contracts and SQLite FTS for lexical search. Do not depend on HelixDB, GraphQLite or a separate graph database for the app. External HelixDB schema reading is excluded under DB-06–07.

STORE-09 [Confirmed]: All internal persistence must be accessed through domain-focused repository/query traits and an explicit transaction boundary. Keep SQL, SQLite connections, statements, row mappings, migrations, FTS and sqlite-vec implementation types inside the storage adapter. UI, coordinators, tools, jobs, router and domain/application services must not call SQLite directly or depend on its public types. A replacement data store must preserve the application contracts without rewriting those consumers. External database tools use their separately permissioned target adapters, not raw access to the internal store.

STORE-10 [Proposed]: Define shared unit-of-work and read-snapshot contracts. Repositories participating in one logical mutation must share one transaction, preserving atomic domain state, history and durable intent, revision checks and rollback. Query contracts carry scope, pagination, stable identity, provenance and freshness. Do not expose a generic execute-SQL escape hatch or one independently committing repository per table. Keep network calls, inference and long-running computation outside write transactions.

STORE-11 [Proposed]: Use one SQLite implementation initially and inject it at the application composition root. Require reusable behavioral contract tests against the real adapter, deterministic substitutes for unit tests and no-inference integration tests for transactions, queues, scoped graph/vector queries, publication and recovery. Replacing a store requires another adapter plus validated versioned export/import or migration, preserving identifiers/history/artifact links and the same behavioral suite; replacement is not a hot-swap or an automatic consequence of matching method names.

STORE-12 [Proposed]: Graph and search queries must observe a coherent published snapshot with explicit revision/generation identity. Commit writes, deletions and publication must invalidate or version dependent caches; rolled-back changes must not become visible. Test same-connection and cross-connection writes, read snapshots, rollback followed by a new commit, deletion and restart. Scope and overlay filtering must apply before graph expansion or vector materialization; caches must not serve as permission boundaries.

STORE-13 [Confirmed]: After restoring an application backup, keep restored schedules and keep-working stopped until the user explicitly reactivates them. Restoring saved enabled states must not start automation or replay old work. Feature and issue work still require explicit selective Continue, and reactivation must reconcile external effects and preserve existing pauses, approvals, budgets and permissions. This is a restore-specific exception to normal scheduled-run resumption on reopening.

HISTORY-01 [Confirmed]: From a feature, task, or related project work, the user must be able to browse the full linked history of coordinators and workers, transcripts, tool actions, Git actions, reviews, merge requests or PRs, decisions, and outcomes.

HISTORY-02 [Proposed]: History must be a durable queryable relationship graph and event record, not a concatenated log alone. Events must identify actor, work scope, operation, timestamp, relevant repository and revision, and linked evidence. Corrections and reversals must preserve prior records.

ART-01 [Confirmed]: Every project must have a local artifact store for screenshots, files, reports and other work outputs. Agents must be able to save, discover and read artifacts through first-class tools and share stable references with other agents and humans. Humans must be able to add and inspect files through the UI. Artifacts must retain explicit links to their originating project and, where applicable, feature and task, with navigation from that work to the artifact and back. Later reuse must preserve those origin links.

ART-02 [Proposed]: Give each artifact stable identity and metadata for name, media type, size, tags, creation time, producing agent/session, feature/task and relevant repository revision. Preserve source relationships and versions instead of silently overwriting referenced evidence. Show attachments in conversations, task/feature history and a searchable project Artifacts view, with image/text previews and file open/export controls.

ART-03 [Proposed]: Store artifact contents as local files managed outside disposable worktrees, SQLite metadata and graph provenance links. Publish complete files atomically and preserve references across restart, agent handoff and Git cleanup. Feature completion must not delete its artifacts when branches and worktrees are removed. No separate object-storage server or cloud account is required.

ART-04 [Proposed]: Artifact access must honor project scope and effective tool policy, including read-only reviewers. Supply bounded previews or file references to agents rather than inserting every file into model context. Define storage location, quotas and deletion behavior in Settings; retain artifacts until explicitly deleted under ART-05 and show disk/write failures. Include contents and metadata in backup/restore and avoid silently deleting referenced evidence.

ART-05 [Confirmed]: Keep project artifacts until explicitly deleted. Automatic expiration or cleanup must be disabled by default; artifact age, feature completion, worktree cleanup and storage pressure must not silently remove retained files. Storage limits must produce visible status rather than implicit deletion.

OP-01 [Confirmed]: Retained CodeGraph operations must be manually invokable in the app. The user must not need to ask an agent or run the old service to perform them. Manual and scheduled invocation must use the same validated operations as agents where applicable.

OP-02 [Proposed]: Inventory the retained operations and jobs before implementation scope is frozen. Candidate operations include repository discovery/indexing/reindexing, schema sync, selected analysis, graph linking/community detection, embeddings, and maintenance. Show prerequisites, target scope, progress, cancellation, actual outcome, and recovery actions.

OP-03 [Confirmed]: Do not port or bundle CodeGraph’s legacy Shortcut or RabbitMQ integrations into DevWorks. Neither service may become a core application dependency. Preserve general outgoing MCP client support and the user-requested incoming DevWorks MCP server under MCP-01/07. Imported work/history may retain historical source references without requiring a live legacy connector. Internal asynchronous delivery uses the native application/runtime and durable persistence contracts rather than RabbitMQ.

ARCH-07 [Confirmed]: Keep the architecture clean and purposeful: give each component a clear responsibility, make dependency directions and ownership explicit, avoid redundant code and duplicated authoritative state, and reuse common implementations wherever behavior is genuinely shared. UI actions and agent tools should reuse the same application capabilities. Prefer the minimum abstraction that solves an established need; reuse must not become speculative frameworks, unnecessary layers or forced inheritance. Record the rationale for important boundaries and tradeoffs.

ARCH-08 [Confirmed]: Design every important part of the code to be testable. Separate core decisions and state transitions from side effects through explicit, replaceable boundaries for storage, provider transport, processes, files, clocks and other nondeterministic inputs where needed. Important logic must be exercisable without launching the desktop UI, connecting to a real provider or relying on global mutable state. Define contracts that allow components to be tested independently and in combination without duplicating production logic in test-only implementations.

features.title: Execution controls and permissions
goals: Pause, resume, approve and constrain agent execution while preserving ownership and in-flight outcomes.

requirements.text: CONTROL-01 [Confirmed]: The user must be able to inspect any active work, its current step, assigned agents, transcripts, tool calls, process output, changes, and results, and interrupt to change direction. The app must not become a closed pipeline whose internal progress is inaccessible.

CONTROL-02 [Confirmed]: A human instruction must remain linked to the affected feature or assignment and its coordinator transcript. The UI must show that the instruction was sent, acknowledged, and incorporated, rather than silently treating typed text as an executed control action.

CONTROL-03 [Proposed]: Pause must stop new dispatch and request safe interruption of active work. Confirmed project archival is an exception under WORK-16: stop immediately without waiting for a safe step. The app must distinguish requested pause, acknowledged pause, and work that has not yet stopped. Cancellation must propagate to owned child processes and streams where supported; incomplete external effects must be reconciled.

CONTROL-04 [Proposed]: A redirect must invalidate or supersede incompatible queued work and context at a controlled revision boundary. Late agent results from an older plan must not overwrite newer human edits or be accepted as current completion evidence.

CONTROL-05 [Proposed]: After crash, quit, sleep, connectivity loss, or provider exhaustion, the app must retain conversations, assignments, queue state, checkpoints, outstanding decisions, and known external effects. Resume behavior must be explicit and must not assume an abandoned process completed or did nothing.

CONTROL-06 [Proposed]: Restart must reconcile leases and externally running processes or Git operations before resuming writes. Retries must be bounded and categorized by cause; repeated deterministic failures must stop or escalate with a useful explanation.

CONTROL-07 [Proposed]: A user must be able to inspect why work is paused, blocked, waiting on capacity, rate-limited, failed, or complete. Continue must not erase the condition that prevented progress or bypass an unresolved decision.

CONTROL-08 [Confirmed]: Closing the main application window must pause active agents and background jobs, persist their work and execution state, and exit the application. Work must not continue behind a menu-bar or tray icon after window close. Scheduled jobs do not execute while the app is exited. This explicit shutdown applies to all work; decision escalations remain task-scoped.

CONTROL-09 [Proposed]: Shutdown must stop new dispatch, request safe interruption, retain transcripts, checkpoints and queue state, and clean up owned child processes and provider streams with a bounded shutdown policy. In-flight external effects that cannot be confirmed must be marked for reconciliation rather than assumed undone or complete. Feature and issue work require manual resumption on reopening. Enabled maintenance/inference schedules reactivate on reopening, skipping missed occurrences. Interrupted maintenance/inference runs resume automatically; independent pauses, budget holds and approval waits remain. Feature and issue agents still require manual Continue.

CONTROL-10 [Confirmed]: After app restart, including a crash, feature and issue work that was active or whose activation was accepted but not launched must remain paused until the user explicitly Continues it. The UI must support selective resumption individually or together; unselected work stays paused. Preserve current instructions, history, unresolved decisions and dependencies, and resume only eligible work. Workspace coordinator chat remains available independently.

CONTROL-11 [Confirmed]: When the computer wakes from sleep while the app remains open, previously running feature and issue agents, maintenance jobs and scheduled inference runs must continue automatically. Sleep and wake alone must not introduce a manual-resume requirement. Work already paused or blocked must retain that state; automatic continuation does not clear a user pause or an unresolved decision. Manual feature and issue resumption applies after closing and reopening the app.

CONTROL-12 [Confirmed]: Paused work requires an explicit, authorized Continue. Start must leave it paused, including calls from the UI, agents and schedules. Agents and schedules may Continue human-paused work only with explicit user authorization; permission to start new work is insufficient. Existing manual-resume rules, permissions and unresolved holds remain effective.

CONTROL-13 [Confirmed]: Continue on a feature or standalone issue resumes its coordinator and all eligible descendant assignments. Child assignments have no manual pause control. Preserve child-specific blockers; continuing the parent must not clear them. Each descendant must pass its own eligibility checks before execution.

NOTIFY-01 [Confirmed]: In-app notifications must surface required input and other meaningful work events, with direct links to their project, feature, session, review, or report. Notifications must be available from the main chat and detailed workspaces.

NOTIFY-02 [Proposed]: The global inbox must support read and unread state, category filtering, and duplicate suppression. Reading or dismissing a notification must not resolve its linked review item. Resolution and acknowledgment are separate operations.

NOTIFY-03 [Proposed]: Notification policy should cover decisions, failures, blocked work, significant completions, review changes, budget or authentication problems, and dreaming reports. Feature and issue completion presentation follows confirmed NOTIFY-05. Severity, quiet preferences, aggregation and OS alerts for other categories remain open; required-input OS alerts follow NOTIFY-04.

NOTIFY-04 [Confirmed]: When the app is not focused, items needing user input must also trigger native operating-system notifications where supported and permitted. Respect OS authorization and notification suppression. Keep the in-app notification and approval item available if OS alerts are denied, unavailable or suppressed. Displaying, reading or dismissing an OS notification must not resolve the decision. Native integration and per-platform behavior require validation.

SEC-01 [Proposed]: Use one normal desktop user context. Store secrets through appropriate OS facilities, redact them from ordinary logs, and show what project content is sent to external providers. A separate local web login and OS user switching must not be part of ordinary use.

SEC-02 [Proposed]: Autonomous filesystem, shell, network, Git, and integration access must be governed by explicit project scope and user policy, with attribution and interruptibility. A Git worktree provides write isolation, not a security sandbox. Any stronger optional isolation must not recreate mandatory VM infrastructure.

SEC-03 [Confirmed]: Make agent access and trust restrictions configurable, supporting broad/full-access use as well as users who prefer tighter restrictions. Full access is the initial default for new projects; tighter access remains selectable. Show effective permissions and access mode in Settings. Existing role restrictions, including always-read-only code reviewers, explicit approvals and the prohibition on force-pushing main remain effective; full access does not waive them. Configuration scope and OS-enforced isolation options require architecture validation without mandatory VM infrastructure.

SEC-04 [Confirmed]: Provide basic safety checks on tool calls to prevent accidental deletion of entire drives or repositories. Keep these checks active even for full-access agents. Check destructive operations before dispatch, expose blocked operations and their rationale, and preserve attribution in the relevant work history. These are additional guards, not replacements for configured tool permissions. Drive/filesystem roots remain blocked. Deliberate deletion of a registered primary repository requires a dedicated user-confirmed action; agents cannot bypass this with operation approval or full access.

SEC-05 [Proposed]: Centralize safety preflight for built-in and brokered shell/process, MCP and package tool calls. Resolve actual deletion targets, including path roots, parent traversal, wildcards and links/reparse points; protect filesystem/volume roots and registered repository roots. Avoid relying only on literal command-name or string matching. Distinguish bounded cleanup of owned task worktrees from deletion of a primary repository. Define enforcement for opaque tools and native executable add-ons honestly: harness policy checks alone do not provide OS confinement against arbitrary code running with the user’s permissions. Validate any stronger claimed restriction at the process/OS boundary. Rule coverage, bypass resistance and platform-specific enforcement remain architecture validation work.

RES-01 [Confirmed]: Provide a resource reservation system modeled on CodeGraph resources and holds, exposed through first-class tools and visible in the UI. Support named resources with capacity, acquire, renew and release operations, resource/holder/waiter inspection, purpose, priority, expiry and ownership linked to the feature, task and agent session. Reservations coordinate finite resources such as desktop input, test environments, ports, databases and constrained hardware; they are distinct from per-feature and per-issue subagent limits.

RES-02 [Proposed]: Use a canonical resource identity across projects for physically shared resources, including one machine desktop. Scope project-private resources separately. Enforce ownership and capacity at harness-controlled operation dispatch for resources such as desktop input; CodeGraph advisory holds alone are insufficient to prevent concurrent input. Queue unavailable resources by priority and FIFO within a priority; unrelated tasks continue.

RES-03 [Proposed]: Persist reservation state and use atomic allocation, idempotent retries and explicit renewal. Track grant, release, expiry, cancellation, queue position and unreachable ownership. An expired lease does not prove its process stopped: stop or reconcile old writers and reject stale owners before transferring a physical resource. Show recovery and reservation history in the UI, including pause, shutdown and sleep/wake reconciliation.

POWER-01 [Confirmed]: Settings must provide a keep-awake option, off by default, on macOS, Windows and Linux. While enabled and the app is open, prevent idle system sleep even without active work, but allow the display to turn off. Closing the app ends its keep-awake request.

POWER-02 [Proposed]: Use the operating system power-management facility to request prevention of idle system sleep. Show the configured value and whether the request is effective or unavailable; disabling the option releases the request. Do not imply that it prevents explicit sleep, lid-close behavior, shutdown, or every OS power policy. The setting defaults to off and allows display sleep under POWER-01.

NOTIFY-05 [Confirmed]: Verified feature and issue completions must produce highly visible in-app cards floating at the top center below the global toolbar on Chat and every other page. Cards must not reserve layout space, shift content, steal focus or obstruct essential controls. Stack new messages like playing cards, newest first, with access to expand and inspect every message. Keep each card until the user explicitly dismisses it, including across navigation and restart; opening or reading linked work must not dismiss it. Dismissal removes only that card from the stack and retains the notification in history. Provide direct links to completed work, avoid duplicate completion events, and preserve keyboard access, accessible status announcements and reduced-motion behavior. Dismissal or acknowledgment must not resolve approvals or resume work.

features.title: Workspace and project experience
goals: Manage projects, settings and conversations through the native workspace.

requirements.text: UI-01 [Confirmed]: Chat is the primary app-wide interface. Place existing navigation on the left, the active workspace coordinator conversation in the center, and a right sidebar with Current first and Chat History second. Current is selected initially. Overview remains specific to the selected project. Do not replace the sidebar with a conversation dropdown.

UI-02 [Confirmed]: The center conversation must support a persistent composer, readable messages and tool or result summaries, and links to the work being discussed. The initial state must invite a conversation with workspace-wide scope. Keep the integrated Workspace coordinator header; omit the redundant conversation-name row and Across your projects status strip because Current supplies that information. Align the plus attachment button, model/tier and effort controls with Send along the bottom of the workspace input. Below its border, show All projects followed by the pinned model on the left and the send keyboard hint on the right; omit redundant Workspace coordinator text. Preserve usable wrapping at narrower sizes. Every composer retains attachments under UI-08 and routing/effort under UI-10.

UI-03 [Confirmed]: The right sidebar must provide Current and Chat History tabs without disrupting the conversation. Current shows app-wide Needs you, Working and Recently completed, with project labels and direct links to affected work. Chat History shows prior workspace conversations, the active selection, search and useful date grouping. Keep New Chat in the persistent center header beside Coordinator instructions, available with either tab selected. Tab changes and navigation preserve the active session, per-chat draft, attachments and relevant scroll positions; session selection restores the correct transcript. Feature coordinator conversations remain attached to their features.
UI-04 [Confirmed]: The user must be able to leave chat to inspect a detailed screen and return without losing the conversation, its session selection, or its connection to ongoing work.

UI-05 [Proposed]: Coordinator role instructions, workspace scope, and relevant context must be inspectable. Detailed routing configuration must remain in Settings, while request attribution and cost may be inspected when useful.

UI-06 [Proposed]: Every long-running operation must expose current state, progress where meaningful, cancellation or pause where supported, and recoverable errors. Empty, loading, offline, partial-data, failed, and stale-data states must be designed rather than represented as fabricated success or zero values.

UI-07 [Proposed]: Keyboard navigation, readable focus states, screen-reader labels, text scaling, accessible status changes, and large histories must be supported. Resize behavior must preserve the conversation and essential controls. Theme customization and exact native pane sizing remain open; the shared visual direction follows UI-15.

UI-08 [Confirmed]: Every chat input must accept images and files through a selection dialog, drag-and-drop and paste. Apply this to workspace, feature, issue and every other interactive agent chat composer. Attachments must accompany the correct message and remain accessible from its conversation history; image inspection follows ROUTE-13. Use a plus-only attachment button with an accessible name and tooltip explaining that it attaches images or files.

UI-09 [Proposed]: Show pending attachments with filenames and image previews where supported; allow removal before sending and preserve them with per-chat drafts. Store durable copies and stable attachment references, retaining conversation and applicable project/feature/task provenance through the artifact system. Workspace attachments without a project retain their conversation scope until associated with work. Define file formats, size limits, clipboard handling and extraction; show unsupported or failed processing rather than pretending unread content was analyzed. Preserve original attachments through context compaction and provider changes.

UI-10 [Confirmed]: Every chat input must include a selector populated with configured router tiers and available named models under ROUTE-19, plus a separate effort selector under ROUTE-20. Tier Max, High, Mid and Low precede the named model group; Open Router Auto selects the OpenRouter automatic route directly. Selection and effort persist for the chat and are shared between Home and its sidebar. Tier allocation pins its resolved model until changed or replaced by eligible failover under ROUTE-14–15. All requests still pass through the router and respect permissions and required capabilities.

SET-01 [Confirmed]: Settings must expand into a substantial categorized screen covering the required topics. It must remain accessible from the existing navigation while keeping chat as the opening interface.

SET-02 [Proposed]: Settings must provide discoverable categories and search, show configuration scope and effective values, validate edits, preserve unsaved changes, and distinguish configured values from connection health or runtime availability. Exact subnavigation and placement remain design decisions.

SET-03 [Confirmed]: Settings must let the user inspect, edit and save instructions for every agent role, including workspace coordinator, feature coordinator, worker, code reviewer and dreaming. Edited instructions must remain subject to harness-enforced policies, including mandatory read-only reviewers; prompt edits cannot grant tools or override those policies. Active agents adopt edits at their next safe step under SET-04; repository instructions take precedence over default roles under user directions and enforced permissions.

SET-04 [Confirmed]: Running agents must adopt user-saved or approved edits to their role instructions at their next safe step, without requiring a new session or manual restart. Unapproved agent proposals must not take effect. Retain the instructions used for completed work and preserve effective tool restrictions, user directions and unresolved blockers.

SET-05 [Confirmed]: Agents may draft changes to their role instructions, but explicit user approval is required before applying or activating those changes. Preserve version history and provide rollback. Approved changes reach active agents at their next safe step under SET-04; pending or rejected proposals leave the current instructions effective. Approval does not override user directions or configured tool permissions.

SET-06 [Proposed]: Stage agent-authored skill and role-instruction proposals separately from active files, using the approval queue and notifications. Show the affected scope, file changes, rationale, agent/work provenance and validation. Bind approval to the reviewed revision; changed proposals or concurrent user edits require reconciliation. Record approval/rejection and application outcomes. Apply only approved changes, retain prior versions, and keep unrelated authorized work running while approval is pending.

SET-07 [Confirmed]: Provide an app-wide preferred base directory for local repositories in Settings, with an optional override per project. Projects without an override inherit the app-wide default. Users must be able to choose their preferred repository location rather than rely on a fixed application path.

SET-08 [Proposed]: Provide a directory chooser and editable path, persist the repository base directory and report invalid or unavailable locations. Use it as the default destination for new repository clones while retaining support for repositories located elsewhere. Changing the setting must not move existing repositories or alter their recorded paths. Keep this setting distinct from harness artifact storage and worktree placement. Show the effective directory and whether it is inherited or overridden. Default path and clone-destination naming remain open.

VIS-01 [Confirmed]: Deliver visual documents showing the important objects, interfaces and structural relationships for major subsystems and difficult areas. For Rust, show the actual structs, enums, traits, implementations, composition/ownership and dependency relationships; represent inheritance or supertrait relationships only where they actually exist rather than inventing class hierarchies. Include domain object relationships and key component/interface boundaries with enough detail for agents to find and understand the corresponding source. Distinguish conceptual planned types from implemented code.

VIS-02 [Confirmed]: Document major and difficult code workflows visually using appropriate sequence, activity and state diagrams. Cover coordinator delegation and work lifecycles, routed inference/tool execution, durable state/recovery, indexing and context retrieval, approvals and Git delivery where their interactions are significant. Give the managed executable plugin/add-on system particular attention: installation and compatibility, process/protocol lifecycle, capability registration and permissions, tool/router/native-UI contributions, approval and activation, cancellation/failure, update and rollback. Show important alternate and failure paths, not only successful operation.

VIS-03 [Confirmed]: Keep visual architecture documents versioned alongside the code, with editable diagram sources, rendered views and explanatory text usable by both humans and agents. They must remain locally available, link to relevant code/contracts and be updated when those structures or workflows change. Include them in architectural and implementation planning and maintain applicable developer/extension documentation under the existing offline Help rules. Choose the diagram notation and rendering tools during planning; the requirement does not mandate an OO design, a browser UI or a particular diagramming framework.

UI-11 [Confirmed]: Provide a chat icon in the top toolbar on every screen. Away from the Home chat screen, clicking it opens the application-level workspace coordinator in a right-hand sidebar beside the current workspace. Users must be able to continue chatting and coordinating without leaving the relevant screen. The sidebar is distinct from a feature or issue coordinator conversation and must not replace or reassign those conversations.

UI-12 [Confirmed]: The application-level sidebar must always show the current session selected on the Home chat screen. It is the same conversation and logical coordinator, not a newly created or screen-specific session. Messages, context notices, the active model selection/pin, attachments, drafts and history remain shared between Home and the sidebar. Sending from either surface must append to the same transcript. Selecting a different Home session determines which conversation the sidebar opens next; there is no separate sidebar session selector.

UI-13 [Confirmed]: Once opened, keep the workspace coordinator sidebar open across navigation to other screens, project changes and relevant workspace selections until the user explicitly closes it or returns to the Home chat page. Returning Home closes the sidebar and displays that same active conversation in the normal center pane, preserving the right-hand Current / Chat History tabs and their selection/state. Closing the sidebar preserves the session and its draft; subsequent navigation must not reopen it without the user choosing to do so. Preserve the existing left navigation and the page being inspected.

UI-14 [Confirmed]: Place the app-wide Approvals destination directly below Chat in the left navigation, with an all-project inbox and project filtering. Activity belongs inside the project-specific Overview as a section with filters and full history, rather than a separate left-navigation destination. Keep Intelligence navigation collapsible without losing access to its screens.

UI-15 [Confirmed]: Use the approved Workspace coordinator / Overview visual language across every page and secondary view: warm neutral surfaces, bordered content groups, consistent type, spacing and quieter secondary actions. Integrate each page header into its primary content pane, with one continuous outer border and a divider into the body; do not use a detached full-width header card. Secondary panes start alongside the header. Place inner sidebars on the right for Approvals, Knowledge entries/documents, Dreaming run history and Databases. Complete the same grouping and header treatment for Repositories, Agents, Artifacts, Knowledge, Dreaming and all Database states/views. Overview and Features summary values and labels sit inline with matching baseline, size and spacing directly beneath the integrated header. Left-align the version and update message at the bottom of the left sidebar. Preserve existing capabilities and navigation/selection/filter/scroll behavior.

features.title: Work planning and agent coordination
goals: Plan and deliver features or standalone issues with priorities, dependencies, coordinators and durable agent messages.

requirements.text: MODEL-01 [Confirmed]: Project to repository membership must support multiple repositories. A feature must be able to coordinate work in more than one member repository without pretending there is one shared branch, commit, or PR.

MODEL-02 [Proposed]: All durable records must have stable IDs, scope, actor attribution, timestamps, and revision metadata where editable. Cross-links must survive agent restarts, feature pause, repository reindexing, and conversation changes.

MODEL-03 [Proposed]: Feature workflow, card workflow, and agent execution state must be separate. Pausing a coordinator must not move every card to a different workflow column or imply that acceptance has changed.

COORD-01 [Confirmed]: Opening the app must present a workspace coordinator conversation. The coordinator must be able to discover and inspect every project, feature, card, repository, active agent, relevant conversation, Git action, review, PR, and pending decision within the user’s accessible workspace.

COORD-02 [Confirmed]: The user must be able to ask for the status of any feature or PR, work across projects, active agents, and everything needing their input. Answers must be connected to the relevant work so the user can open the detailed screen directly.

COORD-03 [Confirmed]: The workspace coordinator must have tools to create, edit, prioritize, and control project work, and to start, continue, pause, inspect, or redirect the coordinators and workers doing it. Its scope must not be limited to summarization or read-only reporting.

COORD-04 [Proposed]: Before answering a consequential status question, it must read current authoritative records and relevant provider state. It must state freshness or uncertainty when unavailable and distinguish a planned step, a tool attempt, an observed result, and a verified outcome.

COORD-05 [Proposed]: The coordinator must preserve explicit human directions and explain material consequences of requested changes. It must link actions and status reports to stable work IDs, source evidence, sessions, and artifacts rather than leaving their only record in prose.

COORD-06 [Proposed]: Feature execution should be delegated to, or reconciled with, its attached feature coordinator. The workspace coordinator must not silently create a second competing execution owner when the user asks about work already running.

COORD-07 [Proposed]: Ambiguous references must be resolved from context where reliable, with clarification only when materially different actions remain possible. Routine reversible work within the user’s policy must not trigger repeated approval prompts.

COORD-08 [Proposed]: Workspace conversations must persist independently of feature conversations. New chat must preserve prior sessions and their work links. Starting another workspace chat must not duplicate projects, reset feature context, or launch new agents by itself.

AGENT-01 [Confirmed]: A feature must retain a relationship to every coordinator and worker that has worked on it. Selecting Start must launch an attached feature coordinator to review readiness under AGENT-12; selecting Continue on paused work must resume work with its prior history and current state available.

AGENT-02 [Proposed]: Start and Continue must be idempotent against already active work. Continuing must preserve logical coordinator identity and session lineage, even if the provider requires a fresh session or a different model. The app must reconcile cards, repositories, instructions, and external effects before new execution.

AGENT-03 [Confirmed]: A feature coordinator must plan and manage cards, delegate scoped assignments, use code intelligence directly, coordinate repository changes, monitor workers, arrange verification and reviews, and keep the feature’s status and history visible.

AGENT-04 [Proposed]: The execution loop must cover understanding requirements, discovering current code and knowledge, planning dependencies, implementing, validating, reviewing, reconciling findings, and recording acceptance evidence. Existing dark-factory strategies are references to evaluate, not assumed proven solutions.

AGENT-05 [Proposed]: Worker assignments must identify their originating issue or feature and cards, repository or worktree scope, acceptance criteria, instructions, context, limits, and ownership. Dependencies and resource constraints must be respected before conflicting work is dispatched.

AGENT-06 [Confirmed]: The intended mode is sustained autonomy with almost no routine human interaction. The app must keep working within configured authority and budgets, recover from ordinary failures, and ask for user input when an unresolved conflict or meaningful policy boundary requires it.

AGENT-07 [Proposed]: A coordinator must not mark work complete merely because an agent says it finished, a command returned success, a PR opened, or a child task stopped. Completion must be checked against the approved requirement and acceptance evidence; unresolved blockers must remain explicit.

AGENT-08 [Proposed]: Agent coordination must use durable assignments and renewable ownership rather than transcript-only conventions. Retries, stale plans, handovers, dependency changes, and concurrent manual edits must be reconciled with revision checks before work proceeds.

AGENT-09 [Proposed]: The scheduler must enforce independent per-feature and per-issue subagent limits and coordinate provider capacity, repository writes, compiler/indexing jobs, and other constrained operations. It must expose why work is queued or waiting and avoid dispatching work that cannot run. These operational constraints must not introduce a workspace-wide subagent-count cap.

AGENT-10 [Confirmed]: Settings must provide a configurable maximum number of concurrently active subagents per feature and per standalone issue, defaulting to 10 for each. Each feature and issue has its own independent allowance; there is no workspace-wide or global subagent-count cap. Fewer agents may be used when fewer useful tasks are ready.

AGENT-11 [Confirmed]: Feature coordinators and agents responsible for issues must maximize useful concurrency within the configured limit by running multiple independent, ready tasks at once and refilling capacity as tasks finish. Sequential execution must not be the default when parallel work is available. Dependencies and conflicting writes must be coordinated; a task waiting for user input must not stall independent work.

AGENT-12 [Confirmed]: Features should ideally be fully planned before execution. On Start, the feature coordinator must review the feature and its existing plan. If planning is incomplete, develop what can be planned from the available information, identify gaps, and ask the user for plan approval or more input before executing unapproved work. A complete existing plan must not trigger redundant planning or repeated approval requests where authorization already exists.

AGENT-13 [Confirmed]: After feature-plan approval, the coordinator may adapt task breakdown, delegation, sequencing, scheduling and PR grouping autonomously to complete the feature quickly, efficiently and correctly. Approved requirements and configured concurrency, review and delivery policies still apply. A plan belongs to its feature. Keep the original plan active and approved while a revised plan awaits approval; continue eligible work under it. Approving the revision replaces the active plan; rejection leaves it unchanged. Pending changes cannot authorize new work. Use one active plan and one pending revision, without a user-facing plan-version system. Execution must remain visible and open to user refinement and redirection.

AGENT-14 [Confirmed]: The agent responsible for a standalone issue may delegate scoped work to subagents without creating a feature or manufacturing feature-owned task cards. An assignment may use the issue root and a scoped brief directly; optional linked task records belong to the same project and authorized execution scope. Preserve the parent/child agent relationships, assignments, transcripts, tool actions, changes, reviews and evidence on the issue. Delegated work follows the same router, tool permissions, worktree isolation, visibility and pause/redirect controls as other agent work. Issues use the configurable independent subagent allowance under AGENT-10, defaulting to 10, and maximize useful concurrency under AGENT-11.

AGENT-15 [Confirmed]: A clear, actionable standalone issue may proceed immediately to implementation without separate plan approval. The agent may plan and delegate as needed within the issue’s scope. Ask for input when requirements are unclear or an unresolved decision requires it. Existing tool permissions, user pauses, verification, review and Auto-Merge policies still apply; feature plan-approval requirements remain unchanged.

AGENT-16 [Confirmed]: Provide an optional per-project keep-working mode that automatically selects and starts the next highest-priority eligible feature or standalone issue through next_work(project). Make its configured state and activity visible and controllable in the project UI. Preserve plan readiness and approval, tool permissions, budgets, resource constraints and existing execution ownership. The mode must not resume explicitly paused work or bypass selective manual Continue after app closure. Run one feature or standalone issue at a time per project in this mode. Its subagents still use the independent per-item allowance under AGENT-10–11, and different projects may work concurrently. After reopening, keep-working requires manual restart. If no eligible work remains, stop until manually enabled again; later queue changes must not restart the mode automatically. Keep-working defaults to off for every new project; enabling it requires an explicit user action.

AGENT-17 [Confirmed]: Every newly started feature, standalone issue or task assignment must begin in a new session with clear context for that work, including when launched by keep-working mode, a scheduled agent or a user action. Assemble the relevant brief, instructions, project knowledge and scoped evidence; do not carry over the prior work item’s conversation as the new session’s transcript. Retain links to the originating action and relevant history without conflating session identities. Continuing an existing item preserves its established history and continuity; it is not a new work item.

WORK-01 [Confirmed]: Project work must have full manual visibility and control. The feature list must support creation, editing, search, filters, prioritization, and access to in-progress, paused, ready, and completed work. Project membership and feature repository scope must be editable.

WORK-02 [Confirmed]: Each feature must have a visible Kanban board for planning cards. Humans and agents must be able to create, edit, reprioritize, assign and move tasks, and add or remove task-blocking dependencies through shared operations. This includes standalone issues and tasks in different features of the same project. Priority selects among eligible tasks; an unresolved prerequisite keeps a dependent task blocked regardless of priority. Accessible controls must accompany drag and drop.

WORK-03 [Confirmed]: All core project, feature, and card management operations exposed to the user must also be controllable through first-class agent tools, using the same domain rules. An agent action must appear in the same board and history as a manual action.

WORK-04 [Proposed]: A feature must hold requirements, acceptance criteria, description, priority, workflow state, repository scope, coordinator relationship, and related artifacts. A planning card must hold its own type, description, priority, workflow state, assignment, dependency links, acceptance criteria, and repository context.

WORK-05 [Proposed]: Dependency checks must prevent invalid cycles and identify blocked or stale prerequisites. A manually completed card must remain distinguishable from completion supported by verified acceptance evidence where those differ.

WORK-06 [Proposed]: Concurrent edits must use revision checks. A stale manual form or late agent update must be refused or explicitly reconciled while preserving the user’s draft. Silent last-write-wins behavior is unacceptable for instructions, planning state, and conflict resolutions.

WORK-07 [Proposed]: Ordinary archiving or removing work from a current view must preserve its history and links. Permanent project deletion is a separate explicit action under WORK-15. Repository removal from a project must not delete files, branches, transcripts, or evidence, and must explain active references before changing membership.

WORK-08 [Confirmed]: The user must always be able to refine a feature plan, both before execution and while agents are working, through direct management controls or coordinator conversation. Refinements must remain linked to the feature and its plan/history. The feature coordinator must review and incorporate changes into the current plan rather than treating the initial plan as permanently fixed.

WORK-09 [Confirmed]: Provide next_work(project, feature = null). Project is required. With feature omitted or null, select the highest-priority eligible feature or standalone issue from one project queue. Feature selection requires approval for implementation; skip incomplete or unapproved plans. Explicit Start may still initiate feature planning. Feature tasks are not separate project-queue candidates; with feature supplied, select the highest-priority eligible task within that feature and project. Scheduled agents may allocate/start work under these rules. Clear actionable standalone issues retain their existing no-separate-plan-approval policy.

WORK-10 [Proposed]: Allocate the highest-priority eligible work atomically with durable caller/session ownership; concurrent callers must not receive the same assignment. Use runtime request identities for idempotent retries, and expose selection/assignment, work kind/ID, version and no-eligible-work reasons. Validate that a feature belongs to the project. Respect dependencies, active ownership, explicit pauses, budget holds and approval waits. Define stable priority tie-breaking and lease/recovery semantics. Selection/claim and execution start are distinct; use the existing Start/coordinator path without duplicate coordinators or silently resuming user-paused features. Transfer ownership visibly to the feature coordinator or assigned worker and retain schedule/run provenance, context and Git/history links.

WORK-11 [Confirmed]: Every task belongs to a project and may optionally belong to a feature; standalone tasks are issues with the same durable identity. Humans and agents can create, manage and directly start tasks without requiring a feature, retaining their sessions, transcripts, Git/review, artifacts and activity history. Humans and agents may link and unlink issues. Linking makes resolution part of feature delivery and authorizes that addition without revised-plan approval. An existing agent notifies the feature coordinator and continues; otherwise the coordinator launches or resumes work when eligible. Existing pauses and blockers remain. Unlinking pauses work until manually resumed. Future spending uses the feature budget; earlier costs remain attributed where incurred. Keep existing branches/workspaces; the coordinator owns integration. Direct feature transfers continue under the new coordinator/budget while retaining holds.

WORK-12 [Proposed]: Provide project issue browsing/filtering, New issue with optional feature membership, and shared UI/chat/tool set/clear operations guarded by work revisions and project membership. Capture title, description/reproduction, expected/actual behavior where known, priority, status, acceptance criteria, repositories and source issue. Preserve one identity and its agent/session, transcript, Git/review, artifacts and history across association changes. Reconcile queues, supervisor responsibility, budget attribution and delivery routing without duplicate execution. Feature-linked work uses coordinator delivery; standalone work uses existing issue policies. Editable task details expose priority, blockers, Start/Pause/Continue, agents and history. Unlink uses a durable pause; relinking cannot clear it. Issue restart, concurrency and delegation retain CONTROL-10, AGENT-10–11 and AGENT-14.

WORK-13 [Confirmed]: Support custom Kanban columns and status names per project. Users must be able to manage their project workflow instead of being restricted to fixed global columns. Feature boards and project issues must use the applicable project statuses, with the same workflow available to agents through first-class tools.

WORK-14 [Proposed]: Give project statuses stable identities and explicit workflow semantics for allocation, readiness, review and completion; agents and next_work must not infer behavior solely from editable display names. Provide column creation, renaming and ordering with equivalent tool operations. Removing an occupied status requires an explicit destination for affected work, preserving history. Keep workflow status separate from execution pause/wait state; moving a card must not bypass plan approval, checks, reviews or merge policy. Refine the exact status mapping and transition rules before implementation.

WORK-15 [Confirmed]: Removing a project from active management must archive its records and history by default. Preserve its work records, linked agent sessions, transcripts, decisions, Git/review history and evidence under the existing retention rules. Permanent deletion must be a separate explicit action, never a side effect of archiving or ordinary project removal. Provide the same project-management behavior through the UI and permitted first-class tools under WORK-03.

WORK-16 [Confirmed]: If any agents are actively working on a project when archival is requested, warn the user and ask whether they are sure they want to archive it before proceeding. Declining leaves the project and its work unchanged. On confirmation, stop all project work immediately: block new dispatch and interrupt active coordinators, subagents, inference/tool operations, owned processes and background work without waiting for a safe step, task completion or a cooperative checkpoint. Archived projects must not start new work through keep-working, project schedules or other dispatch paths. Retain recorded history and interrupted-work state; unrelated projects continue. This applies to archival initiated through the UI or agent tools. Restoring an archived project must leave its work, keep-working mode and project schedules stopped until the user explicitly reactivates them. Restoration alone must not resume execution.

WORK-17 [Confirmed]: Permanent project deletion must remove only its harness data and artifacts. Leave local repositories, including their files, worktrees and branches, and all GitHub resources untouched. Deletion must not trigger repository cleanup or remote GitHub mutations. Apply the same boundary to the UI and permitted agent tools; ordinary archival remains nondestructive under WORK-15. Preserve shared artifacts while another project still references them. Shared-data ownership and deletion mechanics remain to be specified.

COORD-09 [Confirmed]: The application-level coordinator receives host-authored screen context when its sidebar opens and when the viewed screen or meaningful selection changes while that sidebar is open. Opening injects the current screen without replaying navigation performed while closed. Closed-sidebar browsing and returning to Home chat must not append navigation notices. Do not create a new coordinator/session or duplicate a notice for an unchanged re-render. Home and sidebar views display only the most recent screen-context notice for the selected conversation; user, assistant and tool messages remain in order. Keep all recorded screen notices unchanged in the append-only transcript and provider history; consolidation is a display projection only, preserving the stable prompt prefix. Notices remain bounded and attributed, with local Help and relevant enabled-tool references under COORD-10.

COORD-10 [Confirmed]: Give the workspace coordinator sufficient screen identity and relevant selected record context to discover the information and operations represented there. Link the screen context to its version-matched local Help topic and let the coordinator inspect its available tools and use enabled tools to interact with that workspace. The coordinator should be able to resolve the same project, feature/task, repository, run or other record the user is inspecting, where applicable. Navigation notices are harness-authored context, not user instructions or additional authority; they must not grant disabled tools, remove read-only restrictions, bypass approval gates or start work merely because the user browsed a page.

acceptance_tests: All mapped source requirements and existing item acceptance are fulfilled with native evidence; source statuses remain explicit.
Reuse item evidence for integrated behavior, including shared authority, recovery and UI/tool consistency; design fixtures do not constitute native completion.

features.title: Models, routing and usage
goals: Use the agreed model/providers, routing, context, tools, decisions and cost controls through one native execution path.

requirements.text: ROUTE-01 [Confirmed]: Every application inference request must go through one internal router path, including workspace and feature conversations, worker and review requests, scheduled inference tasks, planning, dreaming, context summarization/compaction, generated titles, semantic enrichment, embeddings, and accepted MCP-initiated inference requests. Agents and application subsystems must not bypass the router to call providers directly.

ROUTE-02 [Confirmed]: The router must choose suitable agents or models for the job through configurable policies. Its detailed configuration belongs in Settings and may remain hidden during ordinary work. Usage and cost reporting must be a dedicated screen.

ROUTE-03 [Proposed]: Selection must consider task or role policy, tool and modality support, context size, reasoning effort, availability, provider limits, cost preferences, and session affinity. A user must be able to inspect the selected route and material fallback reason for a request.

ROUTE-04 [Proposed]: Provider adapters must preserve streaming, tool-call identity and ordering, cancellation, errors, supported content types, and resumable conversation semantics. Retries must not duplicate exposed partial responses or repeat externally effective tool calls without reconciliation.

ROUTE-05 [Proposed]: Show provider waiting/failure reasons and the next retry time when known. Honor router-reported cooldowns under ROUTE-15 instead of repeatedly retrying cooling models. Missing authentication and indefinite unavailability need explicit recovery policy. Do not erase the run or route outside configured constraints.

ROUTE-06 [Proposed]: Usage must be attributable to project, feature, card or assignment where applicable, coordinator or worker, session, request, provider, model, and role. Router-selected catalog identity and any provider-resolved model identity must remain distinguishable.

ROUTE-07 [Proposed]: Reporting must distinguish provider-reported charges, estimated cost, unknown cost, token usage, and subscription capacity. Unknown price must not be represented as zero. A cost preference or routing tier must not be described as an enforced spending cap unless enforcement exists.

ROUTE-08 [Confirmed]: Each feature supports a spending limit or Off. A reached limit pauses further feature inference; Off tracks spending without a cap. Raising the limit or switching it Off must leave budget-paused work paused until the user manually selects Continue. Continue must still honor other pauses, blockers and current limits. Show attributed spend and effective budget state, preserving incurred usage and visible changes. Exact accounting and in-flight request handling remain open.

ROUTE-11 [Confirmed]: When a feature spending limit is configured, begin warning its coordinator at 75% of the budget so it can try to wrap up within the remaining allowance. Keep the warning and remaining-budget information available to the coordinator. Off has no budget-threshold warning. Budget pressure does not waive approved acceptance criteria, required verification or review, or permit incomplete work to be reported as complete.

ROUTE-12 [Confirmed]: Standalone issues do not support spending limits. Track and display their attributed inference usage and costs, without a per-issue cap, budget-threshold warning or budget-triggered pause. Feature budgets remain feature-scoped. Existing user pauses, approval waits, provider availability and selective manual resume after app closure still apply to issues.

ROUTE-13 [Confirmed]: Agents must be able to inspect screenshots and other images directly, including chat attachments and stored artifacts. Route image-dependent inference to a model and endpoint that support vision, through the same internal router. Do not silently omit images or claim visual inspection when no capable route is available.

ROUTE-14 [Confirmed]: Pin each session to its initially routed model. Reuse that pin across turns, tool continuations, compaction and app restarts. If rate-limited or unavailable, automatically switch the same session to an available eligible replacement and persist its pin, as in simple-router; retain it after the original recovers. Manual selection persists until changed or failover; Auto restores router selection with pinning. Replacements must meet required capabilities and configured routing constraints. Restoring a pin does not resume feature/issue execution: CONTROL-10 still requires manual Continue. Capability-change and other recovery mechanics remain open; cooldown waits follow ROUTE-15.

ROUTE-15 [Confirmed]: When no eligible model is available and the router reports cooldown expiry times, wait until the earliest eligible model cooldown ends, then automatically recheck availability and reconnect through the router. This temporary wait alone must not require manual Continue. If cooldowns change, honor the updated availability rather than repeatedly retrying early. Pin any replacement under ROUTE-14. Existing user pauses, approval waits, budget holds and app-restart manual-resume rules still apply. Recovery without a reported availability time remains open.

ROUTE-09 [Confirmed]: Support Codex, Claude subscription, Anthropic API-key, OpenRouter, and generic OpenAI-compatible connections, using simple-router as the subscription integration reference. OpenAI-compatible connections must accept configurable base URLs and model identities, including Ollama and LM Studio, rather than being limited to named products. Local and remote compatible endpoints must use the same internal router path as the subscription and API-key providers.

ROUTE-10 [Confirmed]: Use simple-router as the reference for provider connection and authentication behavior: Codex subscription device-code sign-in; optional direct Claude subscription browser/authorization-code sign-in at the user's risk, preserving simple-router behavior; a separate Anthropic API-key connection; OpenRouter provider-level API-key management; and optional API keys for configured OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Preserve connection status, token refresh and reauthentication, credential replacement/removal, model discovery/refresh, and connection testing where supported. Expose these controls in native Settings. Claude subscription is unsupported by Anthropic for third-party apps, disabled until explicit user risk acceptance, and distinct from API billing. Never silently exchange subscription and API credentials or billing. The Rust implementation must not require the old router server or external agent CLIs.

CACHE-01 [Confirmed]: Provider prompt-cache efficiency is a critical harness requirement. Request construction, transcript handling, tool definitions and router behavior must avoid unnecessary harness-induced cache misses. Provider cache availability is not guaranteed; the requirement is to preserve eligible reuse and make its effectiveness observable.

CACHE-02 [Proposed]: Use a stable, versioned instruction and tool-definition prefix, with deterministic tool/schema ordering across built-in and MCP tools. Keep changing timestamps, progress, retrieved context and other live state out of the reusable prefix where protocol and instruction authority permit. Persist previously dispatched message/content boundaries and append new turns rather than rebuilding or extending old messages on each request. Meaningful instruction, skill and permission changes still take effect at their required safe step.

CACHE-03 [Proposed]: Preserve native assistant/tool-call/tool-result structure, stable call identities, content-block order and provider-required opaque continuation or reasoning blocks for same-provider continuation. Persist the ordering chosen for concurrent results. Do not flatten tool exchanges into prose, reformat prior results, or discard required continuation data during storage and replay. Cross-provider conversion must be explicit and protocol-correct; do not assume caches or opaque state transfer between providers.

CACHE-04 [Proposed]: Provider adapters must declare cache capabilities by actual model, endpoint and access mode, including supported enablement, breakpoint boundaries, keys, minimum lengths, retention and usage fields. Apply supported controls without silently sending incompatible options. OpenAI-compatible syntax or a subscription connection does not imply identical cache support. Preserve eligible session/model/upstream affinity within router policy, while allowing justified quality, capability, availability and policy-driven route changes. Record intentional changes that reduce reuse.

CACHE-05 [Proposed]: Compaction at the confirmed 80% threshold remains mandatory. Preserve stable instructions and reference blocks where possible, record the new compacted context revision, and build subsequent turns append-only from it. Cache optimization must not delay user redirection, retain unauthorized tools, bypass permission enforcement, suppress required fresh context or weaken task correctness. Evaluate total input cost and latency, including cache writes, rather than optimizing hit rate alone.

CACHE-06 [Proposed]: Usage and Costs must show provider-reported cached input, uncached input and cache-write tokens/costs where available, with attribution to requests and work. Distinguish unavailable metrics from zero and estimates from reported values. Provide bounded diagnostics for reusable-prefix changes, tool/instruction revisions, model/upstream changes, compaction and expiry where observable; inferred reasons must be labeled. Avoid duplicate sensitive prompt logging solely for diagnostics. Verify prefix stability and protocol replay across ordinary turns, tool calls, restart, retries, instruction/tool changes and compaction; use live cache metrics where the endpoint exposes them.

ROUTE-16 [Confirmed]: Regularly check official OpenAI and Anthropic prices and keep the configured pricing catalog current, with visible refresh status and freshness. Provide manual refresh. Preserve the source and price revision used for historical estimates rather than silently repricing old usage when the catalog changes. Exact refresh scheduling and parsing are architecture decisions.

ROUTE-17 [Confirmed]: Use OpenRouter-reported request costs when available. Treat local-provider usage as free for monetary tracking. For a custom provider, use reported costs or user-configured prices; when neither is available, allow requests and clearly show that price is not tracked, without treating unknown cost as zero or including it in priced totals. Count OpenAI and Anthropic subscription usage toward feature budgets at published API-equivalent estimates, clearly labeled as estimates rather than actual subscription charges. Show the monetary budget coverage and unpriced usage honestly; other budget, pause and permission rules remain effective.

ROUTE-18 [Confirmed]: Retain native SystemOne decision-model support from simple-router, including models such as Jev: configurable endpoint/upstream identity and credentials, enabled/healthy model discovery, declared question-type and image/video capabilities, structured decision requests/results, bounded errors/cancellation and attributed usage through the shared router. Preserve choice, noul, score and box capability distinctions. Decision models are selected by their own model ID, not offered as chat-generation models or assigned conversational tiers. No old router server is required; native tool access uses the same host authority and accounting as other inference.

ROUTE-19 [Confirmed]: Offer explicit Tier Max, Tier High, Tier Mid and Tier Low selections before named models in every chat model selector. Allocate eligible configured members in round-robin order: initial Max membership is Fable and Astra; High is Opus and Sol; Mid is Sonnet and Terra; Low is Haiku and Luna. Include eligible custom models assigned to each tier. Membership is editable catalog configuration, not a permanent provider/model inventory. Select a tier directly without translating a named model to a tier. Preserve the resolved session pin across turns and restart under ROUTE-14–15; round robin applies when allocating or replacing a pin. Named-model selection requests that model directly. Offer Open Router Auto as a distinct explicit OpenRouter upstream route, not a synonym for DevWorks tier selection. Context, capabilities, effort, enabled state, health and current policy still determine eligibility; do not silently cross to another tier or invent support when a pool is empty.

ROUTE-20 [Confirmed]: Provide reasoning effort as a separate selector alongside the route/model selector in every chat composer, including the shared Home/sidebar session. Persist the selected effort independently of tier or model. Advertise and send only the effort values supported by the configured model, endpoint and access mode; preserve requested and effective effort in route/usage diagnostics. A nondefault explicit effort is an eligibility constraint and cannot silently disappear on failover. Provider Default is a separate choice. Model labels must not encode effort, and changing effort must not itself change tier membership or derive another tier from a model name.

CONTEXT-01 [Proposed]: Context assembly must combine the work brief, current plan, instructions, relevant code and graph results, scoped knowledge, applicable lessons, prior evidence, and handover state within a deliberate token budget. It must preserve provenance instead of indiscriminately replaying all repository content and chat history.

CONTEXT-02 [Proposed]: A session must record its instruction revisions, retrieved context sources, important omissions or truncation, and routing metadata sufficiently to explain what information the agent acted on. Context updates and summaries must preserve unresolved constraints and decisions.

CONTEXT-03 [Proposed]: Resolve enforced permissions and explicit user directions before repository guidance. Applicable repository instructions override default role instructions. Resolve repository conflicts by nearest directory first, only within its subtree; at one directory AGENTS.md overrides CLAUDE.md, whose nonconflicting instructions still apply. Preserve nonconflicting ancestor rules. Discover only authorized instruction roots, retain exact source digests/applicability in each effective context and reconcile material unresolved conflicts visibly. Same-level ambiguity cannot grant authority or silently affect another repository.

CONTEXT-04 [Confirmed]: When an agent reaches 80% of the active model’s maximum context, the harness must automatically compact its working context and continue without user intervention. Preserve the complete original transcript and the same logical agent identity and work relationships. Compaction must not replace or truncate the stored transcript; record the compaction and resulting continuation in the agent’s session history. Any compaction inference must use the router.

CONTEXT-05 [Proposed]: Measure context against the actual routed model/endpoint limit, including instructions, tool schemas, messages and tool results with appropriate modality accounting. Reserve response/tool headroom and check request size before dispatch, including after model changes. Compaction must preserve current requirements, plan state, user directions, unresolved decisions and relevant evidence/artifact references. Unknown limits, oversized single inputs and failed compaction need visible bounded recovery rather than silent truncation or loss of work.

CONTEXT-06 [Confirmed]: Automatically load applicable repository and subdirectory AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md instructions. Instructions closest to the target files override conflicting ancestor instructions within that subtree. At the same directory level AGENTS.md wins conflicts; CLAUDE.md adds nonconflicting guidance. Repository instructions override default role instructions. User directions and enforced permissions remain above all file instructions. Preserve path applicability across multiple directories/repositories; files cannot grant tool authority.

TOOL-01 [Confirmed]: Users must be able to manage which tools agents can access, primarily through Settings. Management must cover built-in application tools, tools supplied by MCP servers and package-provided tools.

TOOL-02 [Proposed]: The effective tool set must be inspectable for an agent/session, derived from the shared selection under TOOL-04 and the mandatory reviewer restriction under TOOL-05. MCP defaults follow MCP-06. Shell/process and web defaults follow TOOL-06 and TOOL-08. Define remaining built-in defaults, denial precedence, and effects on queued and active runs. Disabled tools must be enforced at invocation time rather than merely omitted from prompts.

TOOL-03 [Proposed]: Record tool policy revisions and changes with actor attribution. Tool descriptions and schemas are not authority to exceed user policy. Preserve explicit user selections during tool discovery. Define how read-only classification is established, how missing or conflicting metadata is handled, and how later tool additions or capability changes affect saved selections. Initial MCP defaults and selection controls follow MCP-06.

TOOL-04 [Confirmed]: The configured tool selection applies to every agent, rather than requiring separate selections for coordinators, coding agents, and reviewers. Code-review agents must have access to the same selected read tools as the other agents.

TOOL-05 [Confirmed]: Code-review agents must always be read-only. The harness must deny write/edit and other mutating operations, including indirect writes through shell/process tools, while preserving the shared selected read tools. Enforce this for built-in, MCP and package-provided invocations, not only in reviewer instructions; Settings and Select all must not override it. The harness retains review findings and history without granting the reviewer general write access. Fixes belong to separately authorized implementation agents.

TOOL-06 [Confirmed]: Enable built-in shell/process tools by default for implementation agents, subject to configured tool permissions and project scope. Users may disable them in Settings. Default enablement must not grant review agents write access or bypass TOOL-05.

TOOL-07 [Confirmed]: Implementation agents may install project dependencies automatically within authorized project/worktree scope. System-wide tool or package installations require user approval before execution. Configured permissions and read-only reviewer restrictions still apply. Record installation actions and approval outcomes in the associated work history.

TOOL-08 [Confirmed]: Provide built-in web search and page-fetching tools, including documentation retrieval, enabled by default. Apply shared tool selection and invocation permissions, including access for read-only review agents. Retain tool activity, source URLs and results in the responsible agent/work history.

TOOL-09 [Confirmed]: Independent tool calls must keep running when another call fails or requires approval, unless that failure makes their execution unsafe or invalid. Hold or cancel only affected calls and their actual dependents. Preserve completed results and reconcile uncertain effects before retry. Existing parent pauses and tool permissions remain effective.
