features.title: Code and database intelligence
goals: Inspect and query code and database structure across supported languages and repository/worktree views.

requirements.text: CODE-01 [Confirmed]: Tree-sitter must supply baseline structural parsing across project languages. Core code discovery must remain available without optional compiler-backed tooling. Grammar coverage must be explicit: unsupported grammars must yield an honest text-level fallback, not a false claim of semantic support.

CODE-02 [Proposed]: Baseline indexing must discover files, structural definitions, source spans, imports, and relationships that can be supported by the grammar and extractor. It must attach repository and revision provenance and identify inferred or unresolved relationships.

CODE-03 [Confirmed]: Optional semantic support must accept SCIP indexes and enrich the baseline with compiler-backed symbol and reference information. Language packs may also adapt native compiler index formats into the shared code graph, including Swift index stores; SCIP is not the only permitted input. SCIP is an interchange format, not a replacement parser or a guarantee that every language has an available indexer. All adapters must preserve source provenance and report supported and missing capabilities.

CODE-04 [Confirmed]: Provide optional compiler-backed semantic language packs for .NET, TypeScript, Swift and Rust. Each pack must declare its supported languages, project types, platforms, toolchain/runtime prerequisites and semantic capabilities. Missing or disabled packs must not prevent application startup or Tree-sitter baseline use. Pack installation does not replace the project toolchain or guarantee that every project can be indexed; unsupported configurations and partial results must be explicit.

CODE-05 [Proposed]: Indexing must support incremental updates, file deletion and rename reconciliation, cancellation, progress, failure reporting, and a manual rebuild. Semantic data must record its source revision and must not silently appear current after incompatible source changes.

CODE-06 [Confirmed]: CodeGraph-style discovery and context tools must be first-class agent capabilities: structural search, graph traversal, architecture and dependency inspection, source lookup, and contextual retrieval. Agents must not need to operate the old CodeGraph service to use them.

CODE-07 [Proposed]: The UI must expose repository index freshness, language coverage, semantic add-in state, source navigation, and the origin of relationships used in agent answers. Cross-repository relationships must preserve each repository’s own revision identity.

CODE-08 [Proposed]: Indexing and semantic helpers must have bounded concurrency, memory policies, deadlines, and process-tree cancellation. Deterministic failures must not drive endless retries or leave orphan compiler processes running.

CODE-09 [Confirmed]: Preserve CodeGraph branch-overlay functionality: query branch/commit changes over the repository baseline without modifying its default-branch index. Automatically include each agent’s uncommitted worktree changes in its graph view, isolated from main and every other worktree. Apply the view consistently to graph search, symbol/source lookup, traversal, dependency/impact inspection and context retrieval. Represent additions, modifications, deletions and renames. Retain repository, branch/commit and worktree provenance, visible freshness and coverage, and inspectable overlay lifecycle and failures.

CODE-10 [Proposed]: Identify overlay snapshots by repository, base/head revisions, worktree and local-content version; include staged, unstaged and indexable untracked changes. Select the agent’s own view automatically, with explicit scope for inspecting other views. Incrementally compose changed nodes/edges over unchanged baseline data, hide deleted or renamed-away data, and preserve relation confidence and unresolved links. Publish consistent snapshots atomically; baseline movement or concurrent edits must trigger reconciliation and visible stale/indexing state. Never silently answer a scoped query from main or another worktree, or present baseline-only analysis or stale semantic data as current overlay results.

CODE-11 [Proposed]: Expose overlay request/reuse, build/refresh, status, retry and retirement through UI and tools. Show branch/worktree scope and base/head/local-snapshot provenance in graph/source results and indexing logs. Preserve distinct queued, indexing, ready, failed, stale, expired and unavailable states; request reuse must not return incompatible snapshots. Retire derived overlays with owned worktree cleanup while retaining work history and evidence. Define active-overlay retention, expiry and rebuild policy separately from artifact retention. Missing or expired views must produce explicit unavailable/not-indexed results.

GRAPH-01 [Confirmed]: The app must provide a way to navigate code graphs and their relationships, move between entities and their source context, and inspect graph information within repository and project scope.

GRAPH-02 [Confirmed]: Follow the existing CodeGraph repository home and navigation as the baseline for repository exploration. Opening a repository leads to its Overview, with Nodes, Health, and Reviews available directly. Preserve repository identity and indexed revision/freshness, summary and confidence, health and activity indicators, internal code-project analysis, inbound/outbound dependencies, node-type counts and drill-down, and README where available. The workspace coordinator chat remains the application opening screen.

GRAPH-03 [Confirmed]: Preserve the CodeGraph drill-down from a repository or internal code project into a node list, optionally filtered by node type, with grouped node kinds, expandable containers and members, and links to node details. Node details retain qualified name, properties, trust/confidence, source location and line-numbered source, and incoming/outgoing relationships grouped by type. Related nodes and cross-repository relationships must be navigable, with breadcrumbs back to repository and node-type context.

GRAPH-04 [Proposed]: Adapt the accepted navigation flow to egui and the multi-repository project model without copying Angular routing or web hosting. Internal code projects/modules must be distinguished from top-level work projects that group repositories. Preserve repository context across home, list and detail views; provide return navigation to the originating workspace. Extra graph visualization controls and saved views remain open rather than replacing the accepted repository home.

DB-01 [Confirmed]: Database indexing must be supported alongside repository indexing. The app must manage database indexing sources and connections, including a file path for SQLite or another supported file-backed database.

DB-02 [Proposed]: A database source must declare engine/adapter, display identity, project associations and effective access, file path or connection endpoint, credential references where needed, enabled state, schema selection, and indexing status. Reuse one connection definition across project associations under DB-09. Creating, editing, testing, disabling, reindexing, and removing indexed metadata must be available without deleting or modifying the source database.

DB-03 [Proposed]: Schema indexing must use read-only source access and extract supported tables, columns, types, keys, indexes, views, procedures and relationships. Report coverage per adapter. Indexing does not read row contents into a searchable data index. Agent queries and data mutations are separate operations under DB-04–05.

DB-04 [Confirmed]: Database indexing covers schemas only and remains read-only. Separately provide agent tools to read and manipulate data. Each database connection defaults to read-only; data writes require explicit user enablement for that connection. Enforce connection policy together with configured tool permissions and project scope. Enabling writes on one connection must not enable them on others. Code-review agents remain read-only even when connection writes are enabled.

DB-05 [Proposed]: Expose database data tools against configured target connections, with visible effective read/write permissions and project scope. Support queries and permitted data inserts, updates and deletes, with adapter-specific capability reporting, execution/result limits, cancellation and attributed history. Enforce read-only access at the execution/connection boundary where supported, including indirect mutations; SQL keyword checks alone are insufficient. Under DB-08, link schema changes to their migration commit or direct operation, recording the fallback reason and outcome. Define transaction, failure/retry and sensitive-result handling without importing row data into the schema index.

DB-06 [Confirmed]: Support SQLite, MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server as target database families for schema indexing and separately permissioned data tools. MariaDB and MySQL must both be covered and verified, with differences reported. These are target connections, independent of the selected SQLite and sqlite-vec internal app storage. Supported engine versions, authentication modes and metadata coverage remain to be qualified. HelixDB and HydraDB are excluded from target readers.

DB-07 [Confirmed]: Do not implement a HelixDB schema reader or structural-inference adapter. The user removed this conditional capability on 2 November 2026. Retain historical storage evaluations only as evidence; they neither enable HelixDB connections nor add an internal storage dependency. Schema indexing for the selected relational targets remains metadata-only, with separately permissioned data tools governed by DB-04–06.

DB-08 [Confirmed]: Agents may change database schemas, including supported CREATE, ALTER and DROP operations. Prefer migration files committed to the appropriate project repository through its normal worktree, review and delivery workflow. If committed migrations are not possible, direct schema changes are allowed. Applying either route requires writes to be explicitly enabled for the target connection and the agent to have the necessary tool permissions and project scope. A migration commit alone does not authorize application to a database. Indexing and code-review agents remain read-only. Preserve the associated task, agent and action history.

DB-09 [Confirmed]: Database connections may be shared across multiple projects, with access controlled per project. Sharing a connection must not automatically grant access to other projects or their agents. Resolve the requesting project and enforce its access together with the connection settings and agent tool permissions on every operation. Project access cannot enable writes while the connection remains read-only. Indexing and code-review agents remain read-only even where project and connection settings permit writes. Retain project and responsible-agent attribution for operations against shared connections.

SCHEMA-01 [Confirmed]: Users must be able to navigate indexed schemas, inspect their objects and relationships, and understand their connection to code or project work. File-backed database sources must not require an application storage server.

SCHEMA-02 [Proposed]: Schema exploration should support object search, table/column details, keys and constraints, relationship traversal, source identity, sync freshness and failures, and code-to-schema references where evidence supports them. Unsupported metadata must not appear as confirmed absent.

HEALTH-01 [Confirmed]: Repository health analysis must be visible in the UI, with access to analysis results and the findings that need attention. This is distinct from the health of the app, its stores, or its background workers.

HEALTH-02 [Proposed]: Health results must identify repository/revision, analysis time, coverage, categories and severity where supported, evidence, trends where available, and linked corrective work. Missing, stale, partial, or failed analysis must be distinguished from a healthy result. Scoring and remediation automation remain open.

features.title: Knowledge, documents and instructions
goals: Retain and retrieve scoped knowledge/documents and apply approved, deterministic instructions and skills.

requirements.text: KNOW-01 [Confirmed]: The user must have one Knowledge workspace consolidating memory, knowledge and lessons, differentiated by tags. It must support inspection, tag search and filtering, manual creation and editing, lifecycle changes, and source evidence. Agents must use the same connected knowledge system through tools.

KNOW-02 [Proposed]: Memory must represent entities and atomic claims with predicates, values, scope, evidence, author or agent provenance, confidence, timestamps, and revision history. Conflicting observations must remain inspectable until resolved; confidence must not be presented as proof.

KNOW-03 [Proposed]: Knowledge must support goals, decisions, constraints, facts, gotchas, attempts, architecture notes, and lessons, with active, superseded, or retracted lifecycle states as appropriate. Verification must record the evidence and source revision used, and later source changes must be able to mark entries stale.

KNOW-04 [Confirmed]: Lessons and rules must be visible with their origin, applicability, recurrence, challenges, and relationship to the work where they were learned or used. Agents must be able to retrieve and manage them through tools.

KNOW-05 [Proposed]: The lesson lifecycle must distinguish candidate evidence, proposed rules, effective rules, and rejected proposals. Human instructions, review-derived lessons, and repeated corrections must retain their distinct provenance; recurrence alone must not be treated as proof of effectiveness.

KNOW-06 [Proposed]: Rule delivery must be inspectable: the app must record which relevant rules and revisions were supplied to a session. It must expose whether a lesson has been addressed in code, instructions, a skill, documentation, or a test, and surface unmatched or unlearned evidence where useful.

KNOW-07 [Confirmed]: General lessons must be available across projects automatically without manual sharing or promotion for each project. Project-specific knowledge and conventions must remain scoped to their project. Shared lessons must retain their origin and applicability; automatic availability does not make every lesson relevant to every task. Project-scoped content must remain scoped in agent retrieval and context assembly, including when dreaming consolidates it.

KNOW-08 [Confirmed]: Consolidate memory, knowledge and lessons into one Knowledge system and workspace, differentiated by tags rather than independent catalogs. Preserve identity, evidence, relationships, revisions and applicable learning metadata without duplicating the same item across categories. Scope remains a separate property: a lesson tag alone must not share project-specific content. Human and agent tools must support the same tagging and scoped retrieval operations.

DREAM-01 [Confirmed]: Dreaming must consolidate and maintain memory, knowledge, and lessons with visible runs and outcomes. The user must be able to inspect what was considered, what changed, what was proposed, and what remains unresolved.

DREAM-02 [Proposed]: Dreaming must have inspectable base and project instructions with revision history, manual and scheduled triggers, budgets, cancellation, and bounded execution. Every run must record the instruction revisions, source scope, usage, actual outcome, and errors or unfinished work.

DREAM-03 [Proposed]: Dreaming must verify against current evidence, preserve provenance and human corrections, and separate direct permitted changes from proposals requiring review. Dispatch success must not be reported as successful consolidation. Partial and budget-exhausted runs must remain distinguishable from completed runs.

DREAM-04 [Proposed]: Direct changes must have an action journal with before and after revisions and a guarded revert path. A revert must not overwrite subsequent human or agent edits; conflicts must be reported and proposals must remain separately identifiable.

DREAM-05 [Confirmed]: Dreaming must automatically apply consolidations when there is no conflict, without requesting approval for each change. Preserve the visibility and project-scoping requirements. Conflicts an automated agent cannot resolve must enter the review queue and notify the user; independent non-conflicting consolidation can continue.

CONV-01 [Confirmed]: Users must be able to manage conventions. The app need not reproduce the CodeGraph wiki interface; a dedicated searchable conventions manager is sufficient if it preserves the required behavior.

CONV-02 [Proposed]: Conventions must support creation and editing, search, scope and applicability, activation or retirement, versions, source provenance, and agent retrieval. Project-specific conventions remain scoped to their project under KNOW-07. A session must be able to identify the convention revisions it received. Storage/import format and synchronization with existing sources remain open.

SKILL-01 [Confirmed]: The harness must support skills and provide a way to manage them. Skills must be discoverable to the relevant coordinators and workers rather than existing only as hidden files or duplicated prompt text.

SKILL-02 [Proposed]: Skill management should support discovery/import, inspection, creation/editing of local skills, enable/disable, scope, version/source identity, and validation of referenced instructions and assets. Skills are file-backed in the shared and harness-specific directories under SKILL-04. Harness-specific skills take precedence over shared skills with the same name. Referenced documents, scripts and assets are supported under SKILL-06. Refine format compatibility, reference resolution, dependency detection and helper invocation mechanics.

SKILL-03 [Proposed]: A session must record selected skills and their revisions. Skills must obey tool access and user authority, preserve references to lessons they address, and make conflicts with conventions, rules, or role instructions visible. Record skill-version transitions in session history. Apply changes only after in-flight work reaches a safe boundary; do not retroactively rewrite the instructions or evidence for completed steps.

SKILL-04 [Confirmed]: Support using existing shared skill folders from ~/.agents/skills and a separate harness-specific skills directory. Users must be able to create harness-specific skills in that dedicated directory and manage skills from both locations in the app. Shared skills must be usable from their existing location rather than requiring an import copy. Show each skill’s origin, filesystem location, and which version is active. Harness-specific skills take precedence over shared skills with the same name. The exact harness-specific directory path remains open.

SKILL-05 [Confirmed]: When a skill edit is user-saved or approved, running agents using that skill must adopt the updated version at their next safe step, without requiring a new session or manual restart. Unapproved agent proposals must not take effect. Existing tool-access policy, explicit user instructions, and unresolved blockers remain effective.

SKILL-06 [Confirmed]: Support skills containing referenced documents, executable scripts and assets alongside their instructions, in both shared and harness-specific skill directories. Agents must be able to access these resources and invoke permitted scripts. Scripts use normal harness tool permissions and dependency rules; a skill must not grant additional authority or bypass disabled tools, reviewer read-only restrictions, project scope or approval for system-wide installation. Optional skill runtime requirements must remain explicit and must not become prerequisites for core app use.

SKILL-07 [Confirmed]: Agents may draft new harness-specific skills and edits to their own skills, supporting harness self-improvement. Explicit user approval is required before creating or updating the active skill or making the proposed version available to agents. Record the responsible agent, work/session, rationale, revisions and approval outcome in visible history. Existing tool permissions, user directions, dependency rules and next-safe-step adoption still apply. This supersedes the earlier policy allowing automatic skill edits without approval. Agent improvements to shared skills use approved harness-specific overrides under SKILL-09. Harness-code improvements follow SELF-01.

SKILL-08 [Proposed]: Preserve prior skill versions and show changes, rationale and supporting evidence in the skill manager and linked work history. Provide revision-aware rollback without overwriting later edits silently. Record validation performed and its outcome; an agent’s claim that a skill is improved must not be represented as demonstrated effectiveness. Define validation and recovery mechanics while preserving the required user approval for agent-authored skill changes under SKILL-07.

SKILL-09 [Confirmed]: For an agent-proposed improvement to a shared skill in ~/.agents/skills, propose a harness-specific override and leave the shared original and its files untouched. User approval is required before creating/updating the active override under SKILL-07. Pending or rejected proposals do not change the effective skill. Once approved, the harness-specific skill takes precedence over its same-name shared source, with active agents adopting it at the next safe step. Preserve source/override provenance and version history.

RAG-01 [Confirmed]: Provide a built-in RAG system for knowledge from documents: ingest document content, generate and store searchable vector representations, and retrieve relevant document passages for agents and human search. Users must be able to add knowledge documents of their own and have those documents indexed. This must not be limited to developer-shipped Help, convention pages, existing code indexes or externally hosted corpora.

RAG-02 [Proposed]: Expose a Documents area within the Knowledge workspace, backed by the same document ingestion and retrieval operations available through configured agent tools. Support adding local files using a selection dialog or drag and drop, inspecting source text and indexing status, searching the corpus, opening a result at its source passage, reindexing, disabling and removing a document from active retrieval. Include explicit sharing and Move to project controls under RAG-11. Show title, source, tags, project/shared scope, version, indexed time, chunk counts and errors. Imported documents are managed project artifacts under RAG-12. Removing an index must not silently delete an external original or the retained managed artifact; artifact deletion follows the existing explicit deletion and shared-reference rules. A chat attachment is not automatically a durable corpus document unless explicitly added or covered by a configured ingestion rule.

RAG-03 [Proposed]: Use a staged pipeline for supported document formats: extract text and structural locators, normalize it, split it into meaningful bounded chunks, generate embeddings through the internal router, and publish searchable chunks with source provenance. Markdown, plain text, PDF and Word documents are required under RAG-09. Initial Word ingestion supports modern .docx only under RAG-09; native extraction adapters remain to qualify. Routed vision fallback for scanned pages is confirmed under RAG-10. Report unsupported or encrypted sources and failed extraction honestly rather than marking empty content successfully indexed. Folder watching, remote URL ingestion and additional formats remain open choices; no mandatory preinstalled Node, Python or office runtime may be introduced into core use.

RAG-09 [Confirmed]: Support user-added Markdown, plain text, PDF and Word documents for knowledge ingestion, indexing and retrieval. These four document formats are required initial capabilities, not optional future formats. Apply the same indexing visibility, source provenance, project scope and agent retrieval requirements to each. Initial Word support is modern .docx only; legacy binary .doc is excluded from initial support. Scanned or image-only pages use the configurable routed vision fallback under RAG-10. Do not silently report failed or empty extraction as successful indexing.

RAG-10 [Confirmed]: Extract existing document text directly where available, and use a configured vision-capable model through the internal router as the fallback for scanned or image-only pages. Enable this vision extraction fallback by default. Expose the fallback and its model/route configuration in Settings, with enable/disable control. This pathway must not require a separate bundled OCR model or local inference runtime; a user-selected local vision endpoint may have its own optional runtime. Save the extracted text with the source document revision/content hash, page identity and extraction model provenance, preserving access to the original page. Reuse that extraction for indexing and retrieval until the source changes or re-extraction is explicitly requested, rather than repeating vision inference on each search. Chunking and embedding remain separate subsequent steps, and their inference also goes through the router. Show extraction progress, usage/costs and failures; if fallback is disabled or no capable route is available, mark affected pages as requiring extraction or partially indexed rather than silently claiming completion. Page rendering/batching, language coverage and quality acceptance remain to confirm.

RAG-04 [Proposed]: Offer hybrid lexical and vector retrieval so exact names, identifiers and terms remain searchable alongside semantic matches. Return bounded passages with source identity, revision/content hash, chunk identity and heading, page or other supported locator. Rank and deduplicate results, expose the retrieval mode and useful score information without presenting a similarity score as factual confidence. Where evidence supports a generated answer, provide navigable source citations; preserve retrieved source revisions and citations in the session/work history. Do not invent evidence when the corpus has no suitable result. Graph expansion linking documents to code, entities, features or tasks is a candidate enhancement; the precise ranking, fusion, reranking and graph traversal policy remains open.

RAG-05 [Proposed]: Enforce existing project/shared Knowledge scope and tool permissions before materializing retrieved content, including vector candidates, snippets, graph expansion and caches. Adding a document must not make it available across every project merely because it is indexed or tagged as a lesson. Show its effective scope; default project association, explicit sharing and moving are confirmed under RAG-11. Scope changes must reconcile retrieval filters and caches so former project associations do not continue granting future access. Exact sharing representation and update consistency mechanics remain to specify. Preserve the distinction between source text, derived claims and verified knowledge. Retrieved text is evidence and cannot override user directions, role authority or configured tool permissions. Database schema indexing remains metadata-only; this document requirement does not authorize importing database row values.

RAG-06 [Proposed]: Track source identity/content hash, extraction/chunking version, embedding model identity/revision and vector dimensions. Reuse unchanged valid chunks, reconcile edited and removed sources, and avoid mixing incompatible embedding spaces after a model change. Keep failed, partial, stale and completed indexing distinguishable with per-document and per-run logs, progress, cancellation and retry. Publish complete replacements without silently serving mixed source revisions; define retention of prior versions under existing artifact/history rules. Reopening the app must preserve the corpus, completed indexes and attributable interrupted operations; exact checkpoint and rebuild mechanics remain to specify.

RAG-07 [Proposed]: All embedding, query embedding, model-based extraction, reranking, summarization and answer generation must follow the internal router whenever they perform inference, including any reused library or package. Show effective models, provider availability, attributable usage/costs and failures. Precomputed local vector and lexical search must not require a separate database server. If an embedding provider is unavailable, expose reduced lexical-only retrieval where supported rather than claiming vector search succeeded. Help must still satisfy its entirely local offline search requirement under HELP-05; using shared retrieval primitives must not make Help depend on a network embedding request. Route selection and availability of an optional local embedding model remain implementation decisions.

RAG-08 [Proposed]: Keep managed document contents and extracted text in local file storage, durable corpus/indexing metadata and jobs in SQLite, and document vectors in sqlite-vec with evidence/graph relationships in application-owned SQLite tables. Exact ownership, lexical indexing and consistency mechanics remain subject to STORE-03 and OPEN 08. Reuse common retrieval capabilities for documents, conventions and unified Knowledge without duplicating authoritative records. OxiRS is an evaluated candidate for selected reusable Rust components, not an approved additional store or replacement for SQLite, sqlite-vec, the router or the harness. Before selection, validate actual behavior, dependency/footprint impact, supported platforms, adapters, persistence, scope enforcement and recovery with representative documents; add no RDF/SPARQL service or third persistent store without an explicit architecture decision.

RAG-11 [Confirmed]: Newly added knowledge documents default to the current project. Users must be able to explicitly share a document across projects and move it to another project, including to correct adding it to the wrong project. Expose these controls in the document manager and through agent tools subject to configured permissions. Moving changes the current project association rather than requiring deletion and re-upload; preserve document identity, source provenance and attributed move history. The previous project must not retain future retrieval access solely because it was the original owner; any continued access must come from explicit sharing. Preserve existing historical evidence under its access rules rather than rewriting original provenance or claiming prior agent exposure can be undone. Adding documents without a current project and the precise sharing controls remain to specify.

RAG-12 [Confirmed]: Keep a DevWorks-managed copy of every imported knowledge document and treat it as a project artifact. Index and retrieve from this managed copy so moving or deleting the external original does not break the knowledge library. Retain the original source location as provenance without making retrieval depend on that path continuing to exist. Apply artifact identity, project scope, sharing, retention until explicit deletion and shared-reference preservation rules; link the document to its originating feature/task when applicable rather than inventing a work association for a project-only import. Document scope/move operations under RAG-11 must operate on the same managed document/artifact identity. Removing or rebuilding a search index does not delete the underlying artifact. Updating from a changed external original and replacement mechanics remain to specify; retain all managed versions until explicitly deleted under RAG-13.

RAG-13 [Confirmed]: Replacing an imported document must create a new managed version and retain every prior version until explicitly deleted. Bind historical citations to the exact version originally used; replacement must not silently redirect them to new content. Version deletion follows artifact permissions and shared-reference preservation rules, and retained citations must show unavailable/deleted content honestly rather than resolve to different bytes. Rebuilding indexes, feature completion and storage pressure must not expire retained document versions.

DOC-01 [Confirmed]: Document the working architecture in the code so agents and human developers can understand the purpose of every major piece. Provide useful crate/module and public type/trait/API documentation, describing responsibilities, contracts, invariants, ownership, important interactions, failure/cancellation behavior and examples where helpful. Explain difficult algorithms and non-obvious decisions near the relevant implementation. Documentation must explain why and how a piece is used rather than merely repeat its name or narrate obvious syntax.

DOC-02 [Confirmed]: Keep code documentation, developer guides and architecture diagrams aligned with the implementation as part of the same change. Link important source modules and interfaces to their relevant design explanations and workflows. Review documentation accuracy and test impact with code changes; architectural documentation must distinguish proposed designs from implemented behavior. Existing local searchable Help, agent access, offline documentation and mandatory self-improvement documentation requirements remain effective.

features.title: GitHub and autonomous delivery
goals: Triage GitHub issues and deliver verified changes through owned Git work, independent reviews and configured delivery policies.

requirements.text: GIT-01 [Confirmed]: Source control overview must preserve repository boundaries inside a project and feature. Branches, worktrees, changed files, diffs, commits, PRs, checks, reviews, and merge state must be attributed to their actual repository.

GIT-02 [Confirmed]: All agent coding and integration work must use Git worktrees. Each concurrent coding task must have its own isolated worktree for each repository it changes; tasks must not share a writable working tree or edit the primary checkout. The feature coordinator integrates task changes using a worktree. Worktree ownership must remain linked to the task, agent, history and feature where applicable. Preserve existing user changes without requiring separate OS accounts or a VM.

GIT-03 [Confirmed]: Source-control views must support inspection of repository and branch state, changes/diffs, commits, worktrees, PRs, checks and review findings, with links to the producing agent session. Built-in manual staging, committing, branch management and merging are not required; the user uses an external Git client or GitHub for those operations. This does not remove the harness’s configured autonomous Git and delivery capabilities.

GIT-04 [Proposed]: Automated commits, pushes, PR creation or updates, reviews, conflict resolution, and merges must follow configured authority and branch policies. A multi-repository feature must track its integration dependencies and each repository’s result without claiming an atomic merge across repositories.

GIT-05 [Proposed]: Reviews and verification evidence must identify the source revision they assess. New changes must invalidate or refresh relevant conclusions. Successful tool completion must not be reported as passing checks, review approval, or merge success without observed evidence.

GIT-06 [Confirmed]: When a feature completes, automatically remove all harness-created worktrees and local branches associated with that feature across every involved repository, including task and integration worktrees/branches. Retain transcripts, commit identities, PR/review links, and the historical ownership records after the local Git resources are removed.

GIT-07 [Proposed]: Before cleanup, verify resource ownership and integration evidence and stop any remaining writers. Cleanup must not discard uncommitted work or unintegrated commits, or remove unrelated user resources. Record each result; expose failures and a retry path instead of silently reporting successful cleanup. Paused features retain the worktrees needed for continuation.

GIT-08 [Confirmed]: Features must always use a feature branch in each affected repository. Task PRs target that feature branch. The feature coordinator chooses whether related tasks share a PR or have separate PRs; one PR per task is not required. Open the final feature PR to main only once the feature implementation is complete, never as an early task-delivery path. The final feature PRs remain linked to the same feature and its task/group PR history.

GIT-09 [Proposed]: Distinguish implementation completion, final PR delivery, and cleanup in execution state and the UI. Implementation completion permits the final feature PR to main; review/fix/check and Auto-Merge policies still govern its merge. Keep needed worktrees and branches while final delivery is pending. Run feature-completion cleanup after final integration is verified across the affected repositories, and show cleanup failures explicitly. This sequencing preserves the required branch while its final PR is open.

GIT-10 [Confirmed]: Every task must document its associated current worktrees, branches and PRs so the user can easily find where its work lives. Show the repository, worktree path, branch name and PR link on the task, including each relevant repository for cross-repository work. Grouped-task PRs must be linked from every covered task. Preserve historical associations after cleanup and distinguish removed or closed resources from current ones.

GIT-11 [Confirmed]: Standalone issues use an isolated task branch and worktree and open PRs directly to main. They do not require a feature branch. Preserve configured review/fix/check and Auto-Merge policy and show branch/worktree/PR links on the issue. Tasks belonging to features retain the existing feature-branch delivery flow.

GIT-12 [Confirmed]: After verified merge of an issue to main, automatically clean up its harness-owned worktrees and local branches. Retain transcripts, artifacts, GitHub links and complete work history. Preserve unintegrated work and show cleanup failure/retry state under GIT-07.

GIT-13 [Confirmed]: Agents may automatically force-push their own task branches, including after a rebase. Force-pushing feature branches requires explicit user approval; branches outside an agent-owned task branch must not receive automatic force-push authority. Never force-push to main. This prohibition applies regardless of Auto-Merge settings, package/tool configuration or an approval for another operation, and must cover equivalent forced updates to the main ref. Existing repository access controls and branch protections remain in effect; approval does not authorize bypassing them. Record permitted force-pushes, approvals, denials and outcomes in the linked task/feature and agent history.

GIT-14 [Proposed]: Before a force-push, resolve the actual repository, remote and destination ref, check task-branch ownership and effective branch protection, and validate any required approval against that concrete operation. Use an explicit expected remote revision with force-with-lease or an equivalent guarded update so concurrent remote changes cause refusal and reconciliation rather than overwrite. Unknown ownership must not qualify for automatic authority. Enforce the main prohibition for harness-dispatched Git operations, including forced refspecs and equivalent invocation forms. Define preflight, shell/tool enforcement and approval-binding mechanics, preserving the absolute main prohibition under GIT-13.

GIT-15 [Confirmed]: For a feature spanning multiple repositories, all final feature PRs must pass their required checks and reviews before any final PR is merged. Once every final PR is ready, merge them in dependency order. Apply each repository’s effective Auto-Merge, review and approval policies; readiness does not grant authority to merge when that authority is disabled or awaiting approval. Track each repository’s delivery result and the feature’s overall delivery history.

GIT-16 [Confirmed]: Resolve routine merge conflicts autonomously and continue delivery without notifying the user or requesting routine conflict-resolution approval. Concurrent agents working in the same repository are expected to cause conflicts; the coordinator must reconcile their changes while preserving the approved feature requirements. Conflict resolution does not waive required checks, reviews, repository merge authority or the prohibition on force-pushing main. If a merge fails in an unusual way that the coordinator cannot resolve, pause the affected delivery and dependent work and notify the user with the failure, attempts and evidence. Independent work continues; ordinary recoverable conflicts are recorded in history without a user notification.

GIT-17 [Confirmed]: A feature is complete once all of its final feature PRs are verified as merged into main across the affected repositories. Track releases and deployments separately, retaining links to the feature, repositories, revisions and delivery history. A pending, approval-waiting or failed release or deployment must not keep the merged feature open. Release and deployment actions retain their separate configured authority under DELIVERY-09. Feature completion triggers the required cleanup of harness-owned worktrees and local branches under GIT-06–09; retain the feature’s history and artifacts and expose cleanup outcomes separately.

REVIEW-01 [Confirmed]: The app must provide an approval or review queue for conflicts an automated agent cannot resolve. Items must show the competing records or proposed change, evidence, origin, affected project and work, and the decision required from the user.

REVIEW-02 [Proposed]: The queue must distinguish a human-escalated decision from a proposal that an authorized agent can review. Agents must not impersonate a human resolution. Resolution must retain actor, rationale, revisions, and resulting changes, with expected-version checks against the records being resolved.

REVIEW-03 [Confirmed]: An escalation must pause only the task needing user input and work dependent on that task or merge. Agents must continue unblocked tasks in the feature. The entire feature should wait only when that merge blocks the remaining feature work. Resolving one item must not clear unrelated conflicts; existing instructions remain effective while a proposal is pending.

GH-01 [Confirmed]: The app must provide GitHub configuration and integration as a supported product capability, with visible account/host configuration, repository associations, authorization status, and access to linked PRs, checks, and code reviews.

GH-02 [Proposed]: GitHub credentials, token scopes and failures must be inspectable without exposing secrets. Git transport credentials and GitHub API authorization must be distinguished. Use the single GitHub.com account and organization support under GH-03. Use direct API polling under GH-10. Authentication method and additional Git hosts remain open; multiple-account and Enterprise support are not required by the agreed scope.

GH-03 [Confirmed]: Support one GitHub.com account, including personal repositories and repositories owned by organizations the account can access. Organization-owned repositories must support discovery, project association and the same authorized PR, check, review and delivery workflows as personal repositories. Preserve repository owner identity and respect actual account and repository permissions; organization support must not require signing in as another user.

GH-04 [Confirmed]: Always display references to GitHub resources as clickable links to the corresponding resource. Apply this across coordinator/agent messages, task and feature details, source-control views, activity/history, reviews, notifications and other app surfaces. This includes repositories, branches, commits, issues, PRs, reviews and checks/workflow runs when referenced. Use identifiable labels with repository/owner context where needed; a bare resource number, name or hash must not substitute for the link.

GH-05 [Confirmed]: For linked GitHub issues, automatically reflect remote updates in local tracking. Keep intermediate execution details local. Once work is completed and verified, automatically post a resolution summary and close the GitHub issue. Verify and use clarification about the same bug; genuinely new scope or feature requests require a user decision. Remote closure does not stop a verified bug already being fixed or approved/planned feature work. Close the local copy of an unstarted unreproducible bug; retain feature requests for manual decision. Preserve identity and source links; locally created issues stay local until explicitly published/linked.

GH-06 [Proposed]: Persist remote identity, observations, routed local work, import checkpoints and publication receipts. Deduplicate import/triage, coalesce updates and separate remote fields from local workflow, plan, pauses, budgets and private history. Use durable paced intake and outbox effects with echo suppression, bounded retries and observation-first recovery. Resolution publication binds verified completion/integration evidence; uncertain comment/close outcomes are reconciled before retry. Show queued/running/failed/conflicted state and authentication/rate-limit failures. Reopening a remote issue cannot clear a human pause or authorize resumed work.

GH-07 [Confirmed]: Agents verify and incorporate GitHub clarification about the same bug. Genuinely new scope or feature requests are held for a user decision with an in-app notification. Agents reconcile other conflicting updates automatically, retaining both versions, provenance and rationale. If unresolved, preserve both versions and escalate through the approval queue with an in-app notification. Only conflicting changes and affected work wait; unrelated work continues. Reconciliation cannot override user directions, permissions or pauses, or publish intermediate local execution details.

GH-08 [Confirmed]: Locally created issues stay local until explicitly published to GitHub or linked to an existing GitHub issue. Creation/editing never implicitly publishes or links them. After explicit linking/publication, apply inbound updates and verified-resolution publication under GH-05; retain local identity/history and configured permissions. Do not mirror every local edit or workflow status to GitHub.

GH-09 [Confirmed]: Automatically import existing open GitHub issues when connecting a repository and every newly reported issue thereafter. Queue automatic agent triage app-wide, admitting at most one issue every 30 minutes by default, with the interval configurable in Settings. Keep waiting issues visible without starting agents or catch-up bursts. Triage bug reports versus feature requests, verify reported bugs and immediately start verifiable bugs under existing execution controls. Notify in-app for feature requests or unverifiable bugs. Shared repositories have no single issue-owning project: triage routes incoming reports to relevant project context. Projects retain their own issues/features; feature coordinators and the message board coordinate overlapping work.

GH-10 [Confirmed]: Use direct GitHub API polling from the Rust application to discover relevant repository, push, PR/merge, issue, review and check/workflow changes. Use authenticated conditional requests where supported, respecting GitHub rate limits, retry guidance and endpoint poll-interval headers. No webhook receiver, public endpoint, tunnel or relay is required. Poll while the app is open and reconcile remote state after reopening, sleep/wake or connectivity recovery. Remote-state reconciliation must not replay missed scheduled inference runs or implicitly resume paused work.

GH-11 [Confirmed]: Changes discovered by GitHub polling must produce application events used both to notify relevant agents/coordinators and to trigger appropriate repository indexing updates. Events must retain their source repository and relevant work/PR context so notifications and index changes can be inspected alongside the affected work. Code-affecting changes such as pushes and merges must cause the affected indexed code to be refreshed; issue/review-only changes must not require a code reindex. Preserve source revision and visible index freshness.

GH-12 [Proposed]: Persist observed GitHub state and deduplicated application events in the existing SQLite runtime, with separate delivery/progress state for agent notification and indexing consumers. Repeated polls/restarts must not duplicate agent notices or indexing side effects. Deliver events to the responsible agent sessions as inspectable external updates without replacing user directions or clearing pauses; show undelivered updates. For code events, reconcile the affected configured ref/revision with remote content before incremental indexing, coalesce redundant pending refreshes and expose queued/running/failed/stale state and logs. An index failure must not suppress the corresponding agent event. Define initial baselines, event ordering, polling cadence, indexed-ref scope and replay/recovery mechanics before implementation.

DELIVERY-01 [Confirmed]: Settings must provide an explicit Auto-Merge on/off control, enabled by default with project and repository overrides. The target autonomous workflow supports committing, pushing, responding to reviews, fixing findings, and merging without routine human intervention. With Auto-Merge off, the workflow must stop before merge while other authorized work may continue.

DELIVERY-02 [Confirmed]: Mandatory independent code review before merge defaults to on, with project/repository overrides and a separate-agent fix/review cycle. Configured GitHub automated reviews normally satisfy it. Use an independent in-app reviewer when automation is absent, fails or never completes. Automation failure must not indefinitely prevent delivery; fallback still requires complete review and resolution of every actionable finding.

DELIVERY-03 [Confirmed]: Use configured GitHub review automation normally; automatically fall back to an independent in-app reviewer if it fails or never completes. Avoid duplicate fallback launches. Bind review evidence and findings to the exact current head and source identity, including explicit completion with zero findings. Keep actionable external findings in the fix cycle even if fallback is used. Fallback satisfies the DevWorks review requirement without bypassing required checks, permissions or branch protection. Changed heads need current review evidence; all actionable findings must be resolved before merge.

DELIVERY-04 [Confirmed]: Auto-Merge and mandatory-review policy must be configurable per repository with inherited defaults from project and workspace settings. Auto-Merge and mandatory independent review both default to on; project settings may override each inherited value, and repository settings may override each project value. The effective value and source of each value, including local overrides, must be visible. One repository’s review setup must not be assumed to apply to every repository in its project.

DELIVERY-05 [Confirmed]: Every actionable review finding must be resolved before an automatic merge, including minor findings. A severity threshold alone must not permit unresolved actionable findings. The feature coordinator adjudicates disputed or non-actionable findings, recording its rationale in the linked review history. Findings it judges actionable must still be fixed.

DELIVERY-06 [Proposed]: Merge readiness must reconcile the current code revision, required checks, the review source selected under DELIVERY-02–03, all actionable findings, effective policy, and cross-repository dependencies. Apply the effective repository review and Auto-Merge policy to both task/group PRs into the feature branch and the final feature PR into main. Review findings, fixes, re-reviews, dismissals and reasons must remain linked to the feature, PR, revision, and participating agents.

DELIVERY-07 [Confirmed]: The maximum number of fix/review cycles must be configurable in Settings, with a default of 3. Execution must honor the configured limit rather than continue an unbounded fix loop. Reaching the limit does not waive the requirement to resolve every actionable finding before merge.

DELIVERY-08 [Confirmed]: If the feature coordinator cannot reach a decision, it must raise the issue to the user and publish an in-app notification. This applies to unresolved review disputes or fix-cycle outcomes it cannot resolve. The escalation must retain the relevant findings, attempts, evidence, and coordinator rationale; unresolved actionable findings continue to block that merge. Escalation must not pause independent feature work: only the affected task and its dependent work wait.

DELIVERY-09 [Confirmed]: Provide separate settings for agent-initiated deployments and release publishing. Each has Automatic, Ask me and Disabled values and defaults to Ask me. Inherit workspace defaults through project settings, with independent per-repository overrides; show effective values and their sources. These controls are independent of each other and of Auto-Merge. Ask me requires explicit user approval before the action; Disabled prevents it; Automatic permits it subject to existing tool permissions and applicable execution rules. A merge is not deployment or release approval. Harness self-improvement installation/restart still requires explicit approval under SELF-03.

CODEREVIEW-01 [Confirmed]: Code reviews must have a visible management and inspection surface, linked to repositories, features, source changes, PRs, and the agents or users who produced and addressed the findings.

CODEREVIEW-02 [Proposed]: Review views must distinguish local agent reviews from GitHub reviews, support findings and their status, severity, source/diff locations, responses and revisions, and show whether findings remain applicable to the current code. Knowledge conflict approvals must not be mixed into code review state.

features.title: Packages and external harnesses
goals: Extend the application with qualified packages/SDK contributions and connect external MCP tools and harnesses.

requirements.text: ADDON-01 [Confirmed]: Implement optional semantic add-ons as managed executable language packs that can be downloaded and installed without recompiling the main application. The desktop app discovers compatible packs and launches, monitors and stops their helper processes through a versioned extension protocol. No separately administered server, Docker container or VM is required. Harness-owned host and adapter code remains Rust; optional third-party compiler tooling may use its native runtime. Distribute prebuilt helpers for supported OS and CPU targets so installation does not require compiling a Rust crate locally. Cargo features and arbitrary downloaded crates are not the runtime extension mechanism.

ADDON-02 [Confirmed]: Provide a dedicated Add-ons management screen within Settings for available and installed language packs, including .NET, TypeScript, Swift and Rust. Users must be able to install, update, enable, disable and uninstall packs; inspect versions, language/project/platform support and prerequisites; check dependency and compatibility status; configure pack settings and project enablement; and navigate to indexing progress, errors and logs. Show effective availability separately from configured enablement, including not installed, disabled, missing dependency, incompatible, ready and failed states. Missing or failed packs must leave unrelated work and baseline indexing available.

ADDON-03 [Proposed]: Define a Rust SDK and a versioned manifest/protocol describing pack identity, publisher/source, version, host API compatibility, platform binaries, languages/project discovery, dependencies, configuration schema and indexing capabilities. Negotiate compatibility before execution. Use a local process transport, such as framed messages over standard input/output, with explicit request IDs, progress/diagnostic events and cancellation. Keep bulk index payloads separate from control messages where needed. Validate downloaded package identity/integrity and install atomically; distribution, publisher trust, update policy and rollback details remain open. New packs can extend declared host capabilities without rebuilding the app; new host extension points or arbitrary native UI behavior may require a host update.

ADDON-04 [Proposed]: Run semantic packs under app-managed scheduling and existing project/tool permissions. A separate process provides failure containment, not an OS security sandbox. Coordinate helper and compiler process trees with cancellation, resource limits, shutdown and restart recovery under CODE-08 and existing lifecycle rules. Attribute each run to its pack/version, repository, worktree, source snapshot and toolchain. Validate SCIP or native-adapter output before publishing a consistent graph update; reject incompatible or mismatched results and preserve the baseline on failure. Disable/update/uninstall must coordinate active runs and mark affected semantic data unavailable or stale without erasing work history. Define the exact active-run transition and uninstall retention mechanics before implementation.

MCP-01 [Confirmed]: Support both MCP directions: connect to external MCP servers alongside first-class built-in tools, and expose a DevWorks MCP server for other clients and harnesses. Users manage external server configurations and select the capabilities available to DevWorks agents. The earlier client-only decision is superseded.

MCP-02 [Proposed]: The supported transport and capability matrix must be explicit. Configure app-launched local processes and remote server connections where supported, with executable/arguments or endpoint, environment, working directory, authentication references, connection testing, start/stop or reconnect, capability discovery, and failure diagnostics.

MCP-03 [Proposed]: MCP tools must retain server identity and schemas, avoid name collisions, follow the same access policy and attribution rules as built-in tools, and link invocation inputs, results, failures, timeouts, and external effects to the responsible agent session and work.

MCP-04 [Proposed]: External servers may need optional runtimes such as Node or Python. The app must show those dependencies and failures explicitly without making them prerequisites for launching or using core functionality. Missing or unhealthy servers must not stall unrelated work.

MCP-05 [Proposed]: Tool discovery, server capability changes, resources and prompts where supported, and any server-initiated inference requests need an explicit compatibility and authority policy. Inference initiated through this integration must still follow the application router. This requirement governs outgoing client integration; incoming clients use the DevWorks server boundary under MCP-07–11.

MCP-06 [Confirmed]: When an MCP server is added, enable its read-only tools by default. Users must be able to choose which tools are available through individual toggles and an easy Select all control. Automatic enablement applies to read-only tools; other tools become available through user selection. Show the effective selection in Settings.

MCP-07 [Confirmed]: Other MCP-compatible clients and harnesses must be able to use DevWorks indexed code, planned work and Knowledge. Preserve code search, architecture/dependency/source retrieval, plans/features/issues/tasks and their histories, and Knowledge claims/evidence/conventions/document retrieval with the same scope, freshness and provenance as first-class application tools.

MCP-08 [Proposed]: Provide native stdio and Streamable HTTP access through a server adapter to the shared application gateway. Stdio uses a small installed bridge to the running desktop app; HTTP is opt-in and loopback-bound. Closing the app makes the server unavailable and must not leave a daemon or a second store writer. Publish version-qualified setup instructions and an explicit protocol/capability compatibility matrix.

MCP-09 [Proposed]: Incoming clients require individually authorized, revocable identities and explicit project/repository/worktree scopes. Default grants allow selected reads only. Human configuration controls connection approval, credential provisioning, tool/resource visibility and any write grants. Check current authority before invocation and publication; protocol metadata, client labels, tool annotations and resource URIs cannot grant authority. Credentials and private application/package transports are never exposed.

MCP-10 [Proposed]: Allow explicitly selected work and Knowledge mutations through existing typed commands, revisions, approvals, attribution, idempotency receipts and recovery rules. An external harness cannot impersonate a human, self-grant permissions, bypass reviewer restrictions or clear human-only execution holds. Index refresh or inference is an explicit separately granted command, never a hidden effect of context retrieval. Keep external inference and provider credentials owned by the external harness unless it explicitly invokes an authorized DevWorks operation.

MCP-11 [Proposed]: Expose discoverable tools and scoped resources, with optional context prompts, bounded pagination/results and precise unsupported or unavailable outcomes. Preserve view/source identity, citations, coverage gaps and work revisions; support cancellation and durable status/receipt recovery after disconnection without duplicate effects. Qualify at least two independent clients across both transports, including revoked scopes, isolated overlays, denied writes and restart behavior before advertising compatibility.

EXT-01 [Confirmed]: Provide a general harness package system using managed executables and a Rust SDK, sharing versioned installation and lifecycle infrastructure with language packs. Packages may contribute agent tools, commands, workflow steps and verification gates, event handlers, context retrieval and compaction extensions, skills, prompts and role instructions, and native UI contributions. Provider extensions must register through the router rather than create a separate inference path. Support local package development and independently installable prebuilt packages without recompiling the main app. Building Rust packages locally requires the appropriate development toolchain; installing compatible prebuilt packages does not. Core use must not require a TypeScript/Bun/Node runtime.

EXT-02 [Confirmed]: Agents must be able to create and test a package project, explain its capabilities and changes, and propose it for activation. Agent-authored new or changed executable packages require explicit user approval before activation, including updates to active packages. Bind approval to the reviewed package version and contents; record rationale, requested capabilities, dependencies, verification evidence and originating agent/work. Pending or rejected proposals leave the active version unchanged. Package development and tests use authorized worktrees and tool permissions; packaged skills and role-instruction changes retain SKILL-07–09 and SET-05–06 approval rules. Approval to activate a package does not grant approval for every action it later requests.

EXT-03 [Confirmed]: Package UI contributions must use host-defined descriptions of settings pages, forms, tables, reports, panels, actions and status indicators rendered natively by egui. Packages may request host dialogs and notifications through the same application interfaces. Do not require a WebView or exchange egui objects across the executable boundary. Packages can extend the UI within supported contribution points without rebuilding the host; completely new widget types or host extension points may require a host update. Exact schemas and supported component coverage remain to be specified.

EXT-04 [Confirmed]: Package actions must use the shared application command/query and tool interfaces and retain project scope, tool selection, read-only reviewer restrictions, work ownership, concurrency/resource limits, plan approval and review/delivery gates. All package-requested inference must pass through the internal router. Context and compaction contributions must preserve original transcripts, user directions, required context and the configured compaction threshold; avoid unnecessary cache changes and record context provenance. Extensions may add checks but must not silently remove required gates. Managed executable separation is not an OS security sandbox: host checks govern brokered operations, and restricting arbitrary native file or network access would require OS isolation. Document the executable trust model honestly.

EXT-05 [Confirmed]: Broaden Settings Add-ons into one management screen for language packs and general harness packages. Show package type, source, version, contributions, scope, requested/effective access, prerequisites, compatibility, health and logs. Provide install, update, configure, enable, disable and uninstall controls and access to approval proposals. Approved new versions reload at the next safe boundary, retaining the prior version for rollback and recording which package version each agent used. Preserve package state and linked activity through restart; visible failures must not stall unrelated authorized work. Exact state migration, rollback compatibility and active-run transition mechanics remain proposed implementation details.

EXT-06 [Proposed]: Extend the common manifest and local process protocol with declared contributions, configuration schemas, scoped host calls, event subscriptions and package state access. The host owns registration, validates messages and results, and attributes tools, commands, hooks, state and UI actions to package/version, agent/session and applicable work. Separate notifications from bounded decision or transformation hooks; define ordering, timeouts, errors and recovery so a failed extension cannot leave a required decision looking successful. Persist subscription progress and action identities where replay is supported to prevent duplicate external effects. Apply package-version changes at explicit safe boundaries and reconcile state before rollback. Protocol details, distribution/trust, dependency resolution, SDK APIs and native UI schemas remain open.

EXT-07 [Confirmed]: After the user explicitly trusts a publisher for package updates, allow compatible signed updates to activate automatically at a safe boundary provided access does not expand beyond the approved scope. Expanded access requires fresh approval. New or changed agent-authored executable contents still require explicit approval of the exact version and contents under EXT-02, even if signed by a trusted publisher. Preserve active work, prior outcomes and rollback/state compatibility; publisher trust does not authorize future actions outside normal tool, role, work and permission controls.

features.title: Agent tools and automation
goals: Give agents the configured browser, desktop, process, container, web and scheduled-action tools under existing controls.

requirements.text: UIQA-01 [Confirmed]: Provide first-class agent tools for testing websites through browser control and for testing native desktop applications through computer control. UI tests must exercise the application under development and expose their activity and results in the harness. Browser control does not change the native egui UI decision.

UIQA-02 [Proposed]: Use browser DOM/accessibility targets and native accessibility controls where available, with screenshots and pointer/keyboard input when needed. Native automation needs platform adapters and explicit permission/capability status on macOS, Windows and Linux. Unsupported controls or missing permissions must produce visible limitations rather than false test success.

UIQA-03 [Proposed]: Link UI test sessions, actions, screenshots, assertions, failures and relevant browser/process logs to the feature, task, responsible agent and tested repository revision. The user must be able to inspect, interrupt and redirect testing. Record observed outcomes; completing an input action alone does not prove a workflow passed.

UIQA-04 [Proposed]: Isolate concurrent browser sessions and test data. Coordinate access to shared desktop focus, mouse and keyboard through the resource reservation system under RES-01–03 so agents cannot interfere with each other. This resource constraint must not become a global subagent-count cap. If the user is active, desktop takeover requires OK or Wait under UIQA-05; idle detection and approval lifetime remain open. Mutating UI tests must run under an authorized testing/implementation role, preserving always-read-only reviewers.

UIQA-05 [Confirmed]: Before taking control of a desktop that is not idle, ask the user and offer OK or Wait. OK authorizes the pending takeover; Wait defers it and must not be treated as approval. Do not inject input or steal focus while awaiting the answer or after Wait. Show the request and waiting state in the app. Independent feature work must continue. Idle detection and retry mechanics remain to be specified.

CONTAINER-01 [Confirmed]: Provide an app-wide preferred container-system setting with optional per-project overrides, supporting Docker and Podman for projects that require containers. Projects without an override inherit the app-wide backend; clearing an override restores inheritance. Harness tools must honor the selected backend for container operations rather than require Docker for all projects. Container runtimes are optional project dependencies, not prerequisites for starting or using the harness itself.

CONTAINER-02 [Confirmed]: Offer Apple’s first-party container tooling as an additional backend on supported Macs where feasible. Detect supported OS/CPU and installed tooling and clearly show unavailable or unsupported states. Do not describe it as a universally preinstalled macOS capability. Rust host code may integrate with the optional external tool; no Swift development toolchain is required merely by choosing this backend. Validate the supported operation set before claiming parity with Docker or Podman.

CONTAINER-03 [Proposed]: Use backend adapters for image build/pull, container create/start/stop, command execution, inspection and logs, reporting supported operations explicitly. Show selected versus effective backend, executable/connection, version, health and errors in Settings. Record project/work/agent attribution, coordinate shared ports and other resources, and enforce existing tool permissions and read-only reviewer restrictions. Require normal system-install approval for installing runtimes. Do not silently substitute another backend or assume OCI-image compatibility guarantees Compose, networking, volume or Docker API compatibility. Closing the app stops agent-work containers under CONTAINER-04. Initial backend default, multi-service support, ownership/recovery mechanics and container lifecycle across pause, archive and deletion remain open.

CONTAINER-04 [Confirmed]: When the app closes, stop containers launched for agent work. Leave pre-existing and manually managed containers running. Preserve attribution so shutdown targets the agent-work containers rather than stopping the selected engine or all of its containers. Stopping is not permission to delete containers, images, volumes or stored data. Exact ownership detection, stop failure/recovery and restart behavior remain to specify.

JOB-01 [Confirmed]: The app must manage scheduled background jobs, including the selected CodeGraph job types. Settings must expose schedules and controls, while run status and meaningful outcomes remain visible from related workspaces.

JOB-02 [Proposed]: Job records must include type, target/scope, schedule and timezone, enabled state, parameters, last and next run, and linked execution history. Create/edit, pause/enable, Run now, inspect, and supported cancellation/retry controls must be available. Scheduled inference overlap is skipped under JOB-08. Define checkpoint/reconciliation mechanics, failure/backoff, resource controls and usage reporting without job spending limits under JOB-09; missed occurrences are skipped under JOB-03 and interrupted runs resume under JOB-04.

JOB-03 [Confirmed]: Enabled maintenance and scheduled inference tasks at app/project scope reactivate automatically when the app reopens, independently of manual feature and issue resumption. Missed occurrences stay missed: compute the next future occurrence without replaying them, coalescing them into an immediate catch-up run or launching a startup catch-up batch. Runs already active when the app closed resume under JOB-04.

JOB-04 [Confirmed]: Maintenance and scheduled inference runs active at app closure resume automatically on reopening, without waiting for their next due time or requiring feature or issue resumption. Continue the interrupted run with its existing identity, progress and history; this does not replay missed occurrences. Preserve separate user pauses, budget holds and approval waits. Job resumption must not implicitly resume feature or issue agents paused by app closure; those require manual Continue.

JOB-05 [Confirmed]: Support scheduled inference tasks at both project level and app level. Each task must be configurable to run instructions and perform automated actions through the harness’s tools and router. A required use case is periodically checking a GitHub repository for newly reported issues and performing a configured automated action. Project tasks retain their project context; app-level tasks can cover configured work across projects. Scheduled actions remain subject to effective tool permissions and existing approval policies.

JOB-06 [Proposed]: Manage each inference schedule’s name, scope/targets, saved prompt, schedule/timezone, enabled state, routing and usage reporting without job spending limits under JOB-09, with skipped inference overlap under JOB-08 and visible failure policy. Provide create/edit, enable/disable, Run now, inspect and cancel controls. Each run has a linked agent transcript, tool/action history, usage, outcome and created work/artifacts. Persist discovery checkpoints and action identities so repeated issue scans and retries do not duplicate actions. Unresolved actions enter the existing input queue with notifications. Apply no-server and pause/exit constraints, with automatic schedule/run resumption and no catch-up under JOB-03–04; reconcile external effects before retry.

JOB-07 [Confirmed]: The agent launched by a scheduled inference task has the full configured tool access available to an authorized coordinator/implementation agent, including tools that select and start work. It is not restricted to monitoring or read-only actions merely because it was scheduled. It may call next_work(project, feature = null) to select a feature or standalone issue, or pass a feature to select one of its tasks, and start that work. Existing tool permissions, plan-readiness/approval rules and explicit pauses still apply; scheduled execution does not grant a policy bypass.

JOB-08 [Confirmed]: If a scheduled inference task is still running when its next scheduled occurrence arrives, skip that occurrence. Do not start an overlapping run or queue that occurrence for later catch-up. Preserve the current run and expose the skipped outcome in schedule history. Existing restart, interruption and explicit-pause rules remain in effect.

JOB-09 [Confirmed]: Scheduled inference jobs report per-run usage and costs but have no job spending limits or monetary-limit holds. Apply ROUTE-17 reported/estimated/free/untracked classifications. Feature work started by a schedule remains subject to that feature’s configured budget and normal approval, pause, eligibility and permission rules; invoking it through a job must not bypass those controls. Ordinary cancellation, deadlines and resource controls remain independent of monetary limits.
