goals: Install, maintain, document, restore and update the native application and establish integrated product acceptance.

requirements.text: HELP-01 [Confirmed]: Provide Help as a first-class menu/navigation item near Settings. It must open a searchable documentation workspace and remain readily accessible from the main interface. Every screen and Settings section must include a contextual Help link that opens its relevant local documentation topic.

HELP-02 [Confirmed]: Document every aspect of the working system, including every UI screen, action and setting; project/repository/work/agent workflows; planning, approvals and delivery; routing and context; knowledge and skills; indexing and graph/schema exploration; jobs, containers and integrations; artifacts, storage and lifecycle; and diagnostics, recovery, permissions and limitations. Explain actual behavior, defaults, configuration scope and practical use. Documentation is a core product capability and must be maintained with the functionality it describes.

HELP-03 [Confirmed]: Document all supported extensibility points and how to create plugins/add-ins, including harness packages and semantic language packs. Provide developer guidance for SDKs, manifests, protocols, tools/commands, workflows/events, context/instruction extensions, native UI contributions and router/provider adapters where supported. Cover prerequisites, development/build/test, packaging, installation/configuration, permissions and approvals, compatibility/versioning, updates, troubleshooting and rollback, with usable examples. Distinguish supported contracts from unimplemented or unsupported capabilities.

HELP-04 [Confirmed]: Make system and extension documentation accessible to agents through first-class search/read tools so coordinators, workers and read-only reviewers can learn and use the system they operate. Humans and agents must access the same maintained documentation. Documentation retrieval follows configured tool permissions and must not grant authority or override user directions. Agent access must cover UI behavior as well as tools and extensibility, not just tool schema descriptions.

HELP-05 [Confirmed]: Help must live entirely locally and offline, bundled and versioned alongside the app and installed add-ons. Match app documentation to the installed app version and add-on documentation to the installed add-on version. Human browsing/search and agent documentation search/read tools must operate on this local content without requiring a network connection, hosted documentation service or remote search fallback.

HELP-06 [Proposed]: Use stable topic identifiers and contextual links from errors; screen and Settings-section Help links are required under HELP-01. Let agents retrieve bounded passages with topic/version references instead of injecting the entire manual into each session. Review documentation coverage and examples alongside capability changes, and expose missing, stale or unavailable documentation. Exact local authoring format, search/indexing, packaging/update mechanics and documentation checks remain to specify; offline-only content and version matching are confirmed under HELP-05.

PLAT-01 [Confirmed]: Minimum OS targets are macOS 26.2 and Windows 10. Linux is also required, with supported distributions and versions to be determined during architecture validation from what the chosen components can support. Do not claim every Linux distribution is supported. Core installation and launch must not require preinstalled .NET, Node or Python. The same primary Rust codebase must provide the selected behavior; CPU architectures, packaging formats and the validated compatibility matrix remain to specify.

PLAT-02 [Confirmed]: The application must work without an app server or separately administered storage infrastructure. Local browsing, planning edits, and history inspection must remain useful without provider connectivity. Provider-dependent actions must show their actual waiting or failure state.

PLAT-03 [Proposed]: Dependency claims must distinguish the app runtime from optional semantic helpers, Git, repository build toolchains, and optional local inference. The app must detect missing tools and state exactly which operation needs them; optional components must not become accidental startup requirements.

PERF-01 [Confirmed]: The app must feel fast, modern, and lightweight. Startup, idle memory and CPU, installed size, active indexing, graph queries, transcript scrolling, and multiple concurrent agents must be measured separately rather than summarized by a single unverified footprint claim.

PERF-02 [Proposed]: UI lists and transcripts must scale through incremental updates and bounded rendering. Indexing, vector caches, process output retention, provider concurrency, and background schedules must have visible resource controls. Numeric targets and benchmark datasets remain open.

OPS-01 [Proposed]: The app must provide local diagnostics for storage, queue health, orphan processes, indexing, provider failures, and recovery. Data export, backup/restore, schema migration, and update behavior must preserve authored records and explain failures.

OPS-02 [Proposed]: The app must not require a central product account or remote control plane for normal operation. Repository hosting and provider integrations may use their own credentials. Provider connections follow ROUTE-09–10; Git-host authentication methods still need selection and documentation.

UPDATE-01 [Confirmed]: Provide an application update function using GitHub Releases from the repository where this application will be hosted. While the app is open, automatically poll that repository every hour for a newer release. The product repository is SceneWorks/DevWorks at https://github.com/SceneWorks/DevWorks; use its GitHub Releases for update discovery. Update checking must not require a separate application server or a background harness process after exit.

UPDATE-02 [Confirmed]: Always display the currently installed application version in the lower-left sidebar. When a newer release is available to download, indicate its availability in that same lower-left area and provide access to the download/update action. Continue showing the installed version while an update is available or downloaded; only an applied update changes that displayed current version.

UPDATE-03 [Proposed]: Distinguish update checking, available, downloading, staged, applying and failed states. Resolve the correct OS/CPU release asset, validate version and artifact integrity, show progress and retry/cancel where applicable, and preserve the working installed version on failed download or preparation. Update the bundled local Help with the corresponding app version. Preserve work/state and existing shutdown/manual-resume rules during installation/restart; self-improvement activation still requires explicit approval under SELF-03. Automatic background download and approval before installation/restart are confirmed under UPDATE-04. The architecture adopts stable releases by default with explicit prerelease opt-in, due launch/hourly checks, signed staging and approved installation/restart. Native offline/rate-limit, signature and platform installation/rollback qualification remains required.

UPDATE-04 [Confirmed]: Automatically download newly available application updates in the background. Require explicit user approval before installing the update and restarting the app. Release discovery or a completed download must not count as that approval. While approval is pending or declined, retain the running installed version and allow existing authorized work to continue. Apply approved updates with the existing work-preservation, shutdown and selective-resume rules; include the matching local Help version.

SELF-01 [Confirmed]: The harness must be able to propose improvements to its own Rust code and handle them through the normal project feature, PR and review workflow. Use the same planning and approval rules, isolated worktrees, implementation, verification, review/fix cycle and configured merge policy as other project work. Retain linked work, agents, transcripts, Git actions, reviews and evidence. Self-improvement does not bypass configured permissions or delivery gates. Installing the resulting build and restarting the app require explicit approval under SELF-03.

SELF-02 [Proposed]: Represent the harness repository as ordinary managed project work. Distinguish the running application version from the source revision, tested candidate build and merged code; a successful merge must not imply the running app has updated. Link build artifacts and verification to the self-improvement feature/task. Implement approval-gated installation/restart under SELF-03. Refine restart preparation, checkpoint/resume, compatibility and rollback mechanics, preserving other work and existing shutdown/resume policies.

SELF-03 [Confirmed]: Installing a self-improvement build and restarting the app to activate it require explicit user approval. A merged PR or passing tests/reviews must not count as that approval. While approval is pending or denied, continue using the installed version; unrelated authorized work may continue. Applying an approved update must preserve existing shutdown and selective-resume rules. Record approval and update outcomes.

SELF-04 [Confirmed]: Every agent-authored harness self-improvement must include documentation as part of the work. Update the affected local Help, UI/tool behavior descriptions and developer/extension guides or examples to match the change, including changes to harness code, roles, skills and packages as applicable. Include documentation in the plan and acceptance criteria, deliver it with the change, and verify and review its accuracy and completeness. Missing, stale or incomplete required documentation blocks completion and delivery; it must not be deferred as optional follow-up work. Preserve existing approval and activation rules. Shipped documentation must match the installed version under HELP-05.

LOG-01 [Confirmed]: Indexing logs must be visible, including enough detail to diagnose failures. Repository, database-schema, and optional semantic indexing must not hide their errors behind a generic failed badge.

LOG-02 [Proposed]: A run’s diagnostics must correlate operation, target, stage, source revision, attempt, timestamps, progress, warnings/errors, helper output where relevant, and error classification. Provide filtering/search, live inspection, retained run history, copy/export, and links to safe recovery actions while redacting credentials and controlling large output.

LOG-03 [Proposed]: Partial indexing, stale data, cancelled runs, and terminal or retryable failures must be distinguishable. Logs and relevant artifacts must survive restart under a defined retention policy. Jobs run while the application is open, including while other screens are active. Closing the main window pauses work and exits. Feature and issue work require manual selection after closing and reopening; it continues automatically after sleep while the app remains open. Enabled maintenance/inference schedules reactivate automatically; missed occurrences stay skipped and interrupted runs resume automatically. Detailed recovery mechanics still need policy.

IMPORT-01 [Confirmed]: Start with fresh repository indexing rather than migrating the existing derived code index. Import existing CodeGraph projects, features, tasks and their histories. This is the complete selected migration scope; exclude existing memory, knowledge, lessons and conventions. Preserve the imported records and their historical relationships when rebuilding indexes. The exclusion concerns migration only; the new harness still provides its required Knowledge and convention management capabilities.

IMPORT-02 [Proposed]: Inventory all records and relationships within the selected project, feature, task and history scope: repository associations, plans, priorities, statuses, dependencies, agent/session and transcript links, decisions and Git/PR/review history, with referenced evidence where present. Preserve source identities or durable ID mappings, attribution, timestamps and provenance. Use a consistent read-only snapshot/export, validate counts and links, and make import resumable without duplicates. Report missing data or mapping failures rather than silently dropping selected records. Preserve historical code references while reconciling links to fresh indexes. Import must not automatically resume old agents, execute queued effects or treat historical checks as current verification.

TEST-01 [Confirmed]: Unit tests are an integral part of the project and must exercise important behavior, invariants and error paths. Select coverage by the importance and risk of behavior, including work state transitions, policy and safety checks, routing decisions, persistence/recovery, indexing/retrieval and plugin contracts. Do not impose a numerical code-coverage percentage. Every important area must be testable and have meaningful behavioral tests; trivial implementation-mirroring tests or coverage numbers alone are not evidence of correctness.

TEST-02 [Confirmed]: Provide full integration testing of collaborating application components without real inference. Use deterministic provider substitutes and scripted response/stream/tool-call fixtures while exercising actual application orchestration and local storage, Git, process or file components where relevant, with controlled substitutes for external services. Integration tests must not call live inference providers or execute local inference models, including tiny or synthetic models. Test important success, failure, cancellation, concurrency and recovery paths, preserving assertions against actual system behavior rather than treating a mock response as proof of model quality.

TEST-03 [Confirmed]: Real inference belongs in a distinct end-to-end test suite to be set up later, not in unit or integration tests. Keep test classification, entry points and configuration explicit so normal unit/integration runs cannot accidentally execute real inference. When the later live suite is introduced, use explicitly configured router/provider connections and isolated test work/resources, retain attributable results and evidence, and distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unavailable outcomes. Missing live credentials or an unexecuted live test must not be reported as successful live validation. The later suite is separate planned work; it is not required to be set up or run during requirements capture.

TEST-04 [Confirmed]: Changes to important behavior must include or update appropriate unit and integration regression tests as part of the work. Include testability, meaningful assertions and failure-path coverage in architectural review and implementation acceptance. Use reusable test fixtures at stable boundaries without building a second harness architecture solely for tests. Exact test framework, suite organization and CI scheduling are implementation-plan decisions, subject to the prohibition on real inference in unit/integration suites.
